questions.explain: In English, we always start reading at the top-left corner of a page and move to the right, then down to the next line.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: A student sees the sentence: 'The dog runs fast.' How many WORDS are in this sentence?
questions.explain: 'The dog runs fast' has 4 words: The / dog / runs / fast. Spaces between words show where each word begins and ends.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which punctuation mark goes at the END of a question? ❓
questions.explain: A question mark (?) goes at the end of a sentence that asks something. For example: 'Where is my book?'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Look at these symbols: 'dog  B  cat  7  run.' How many of these are WORDS (not single letters or numbers)?
questions.explain: 'Dog,' 'cat,' and 'run' are all words. 'B' is a single letter and '7' is a number. That makes 3 words.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: When you finish reading the last word on a line of text, where do your eyes go NEXT? 👁️
options: To the end of the same line and stop
Back to the left to start the next line below
To the right to start the next line
To the top of the page again
questions.explain: After reading the last word on a line, we do a 'return sweep': our eyes go back to the LEFT side to begin the next line below. This is called left-to-right, top-to-bottom directionality.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: A student sees the sentence: 'We go to school!' What does the exclamation point (!) at the end tell us?
options: The sentence shows strong feeling or excitement
questions.explain: An exclamation point (!) shows strong feeling, excitement, or emphasis. 'We go to school!' sounds excited or energetic.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: A teacher points to the word 'jump' in a sentence. She asks: 'What do we call this — a letter, a word, or a sentence?'
questions.explain: 'Jump' is a word — it is made of letters (j-u-m-p) and has meaning. A sentence has multiple words and ends with punctuation. A letter is a single symbol like 'j.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which of the following is a SENTENCE (not just a word or phrase)?
questions.explain: 'The bird sings.' is a complete sentence because it has a subject (The bird), a verb (sings), and ends with a period. The others are not complete sentences.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: A student says, 'I can find the author's name on the cover of the book.' Where ELSE might you find the author's name? 📚
options: On the last page of the story
On the title page inside the book
In the middle of the story
questions.explain: The author's name appears on the front cover AND on the title page inside the book. The title page is usually one of the first pages you see when you open a book.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: A student sees the letter 'G' and the letter 'g.' What can she say about these two? 🔡
options: They are the same letter — one uppercase, one lowercase
One is a word and one is a letter
The big one is a word
questions.explain: 'G' and 'g' are the same letter. 'G' is the uppercase (capital) form and 'g' is the lowercase form. Letters can appear in two forms but represent the same letter.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Sam had a red kite. He ran to the park. The wind blew and the kite flew high in the sky.' What did Sam do FIRST?
questions.explain: The first thing that happened was that Sam had a red kite. Then he ran to the park. Then the kite flew high. Sequencing shows 'had a red kite' is the first event.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Lily found a little frog by the pond. She wanted to keep it. Her mom said the frog needed to stay near the water to be healthy.' Why did Lily's mom say the frog should stay by the pond? 🐸
options: Because Lily did not like frogs
Because the frog needed to be near water to be healthy
Because the pond was too far away
Because the frog was too big
questions.explain: Lily's mom explained that the frog needed to stay near the water to be healthy. This is a key detail from the passage.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'The lion and the mouse were friends. One day the lion got caught in a net. The small mouse chewed through the ropes and freed the lion.' What is the lesson of this story? 🦁🐭
options: Big animals are always the best helpers
Even small friends can help in big ways
Lions should not play with mice
questions.explain: The lesson is that even a small friend (the mouse) can help in a big way. Size does not determine how helpful someone can be.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Ana woke up early. She saw snow outside her window. She jumped up and put on her coat, hat, and boots.' What can you CONCLUDE about how Ana felt when she saw the snow? ❄️
options: She was sad and did not want to go outside
She was excited and wanted to go outside quickly
She was tired and went back to sleep
She was scared of the snow
questions.explain: We can conclude Ana was excited because she jumped up right away and quickly put on her coat, hat, and boots to go outside. Her quick actions show excitement.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Ben had a garden. He watered his seeds every day. Soon little green sprouts poked out of the soil.' What did Ben do to help his seeds grow? 🌱
options: He picked all the seeds out
He watered his seeds every day
questions.explain: The passage says Ben watered his seeds every day. This is what he did to help them grow into little green sprouts.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Mia and Jake went to the beach. Mia built a sandcastle. Jake looked for shells. Then they both swam in the water.' What did Jake do at the beach? 🐚
questions.explain: The passage says Jake looked for shells at the beach. Mia built the sandcastle. Then they both swam together.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'The tortoise and the hare had a race. The hare ran fast but stopped to rest. The tortoise walked slowly but never stopped. The tortoise won!' What is the lesson of this story? 🐢
options: Hares are always faster than tortoises
It is better to be slow and steady than fast and lazy
Resting is always a good idea
questions.explain: The lesson is that being slow and steady (like the tortoise who never stopped) is better than being fast but lazy (like the hare who stopped to rest).

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'A girl named Rosa lost her puppy. She looked under the bed. She checked the backyard. Finally, she found the puppy sleeping in her laundry basket.' Put these events in order. What did Rosa do SECOND? 🐶
options: She found the puppy in the laundry basket
questions.explain: Rosa first looked under the bed (first), then she checked the backyard (second), and finally found the puppy in the laundry basket (third).

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Marcus wanted to eat a cookie before dinner. His dad said no. Marcus felt sad at first, but then he helped set the table. After dinner, Dad let Marcus have two cookies as a reward.' Why did Marcus get TWO cookies after dinner? 🍪
options: Because he asked for two cookies
Because he helped set the table and was patient
Because his dad forgot he said no
questions.explain: Marcus got two cookies because he helped set the table and showed patience by waiting. Dad gave them as a reward for his helpful behavior.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'The three bears came home. Someone had eaten their porridge. Someone had sat in their chairs. Baby Bear cried, "Someone is sleeping in MY bed!"' Who told the others about the bed? 🐻
questions.explain: Baby Bear cried out that someone was sleeping in his bed. The passage directly states that Baby Bear spoke those words.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Zara did not want to eat her broccoli. She pushed it around her plate. Her mom said it would make her strong. Zara took one bite and said, "Hey, it is not so bad!"' What changed for Zara? 🥦
options: She still did not want to eat it
After trying it, she found it was not so bad
questions.explain: After taking one bite, Zara said 'it is not so bad,' showing that she changed her mind about broccoli once she actually tried it.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'A crow was very thirsty. He found a pitcher with a little water at the bottom. His beak could not reach it. So he dropped pebbles in one by one until the water rose to the top.' What problem did the crow have? 🐦
options: He could not find any pebbles
The water was at the bottom and he could not reach it
questions.explain: The crow's problem was that the water was at the bottom of the pitcher and his beak could not reach it. He solved this by dropping in pebbles to raise the water level.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Every night, Grandma told Kai a story. Kai loved the stories about dragons and knights. One night, Grandma asked Kai to make up a story instead.' Who usually tells the stories?
questions.explain: The passage says 'Every night, Grandma told Kai a story.' So Grandma is the one who usually tells the stories.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Pedro was nervous about his first day of school. He did not know anyone. At lunch, a girl named Yuki asked if he wanted to sit with her. They talked and laughed all lunch.' How did Pedro probably feel at the END of lunch? 😊
options: Happy and less nervous after making a friend
Tired and ready to go home
questions.explain: By the end of lunch, Pedro was talking and laughing with Yuki, so we can conclude he felt happy and less nervous. Making a friend changed his feelings.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Jack planted a magic bean. A huge beanstalk grew overnight. Jack climbed up and found a giant's castle in the clouds.' What happened RIGHT AFTER Jack planted the magic bean? 🌱
questions.explain: Right after Jack planted the magic bean, a huge beanstalk grew overnight. That is the second event. Climbing the beanstalk happened after it grew.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Tomas has a fish named Bubbles. He feeds Bubbles every morning. When Tomas taps the glass, Bubbles swims to the top.' What does Bubbles do when Tomas taps the glass? 🐟
options: Bubbles jumps out of the tank
questions.explain: The passage directly says, 'When Tomas taps the glass, Bubbles swims to the top.' This is a key detail in the text.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'A young fox wanted some grapes. He jumped and jumped but could not reach them. He walked away and said, "Those grapes are probably sour anyway."' Why do you think the fox said the grapes were sour? 🍇
options: Because he tasted them and they were sour
Because he could not get them and did not want to feel bad
Because someone told him they were sour
questions.explain: The fox said the grapes were sour because he could not reach them. By pretending they were not good, he made himself feel better about failing to get them. This is called 'sour grapes.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Ella wore her rain boots to school. Her teacher said, "It is sunny today, Ella!" Ella smiled and said, "I like my boots no matter what!"' What does this tell us about Ella? ☀️
options: Ella did not listen to the weather
Ella wore rain boots only when it rained
Ella loved her rain boots and wore them just because she liked them
Ella was mad at her teacher
questions.explain: Ella's words — 'I like my boots no matter what!' — tell us she wore her boots simply because she loved them, not because of the weather.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Mom read a bedtime story to Leo. Then she turned off the light. Leo closed his eyes.' What was the LAST thing that happened?
questions.explain: The events in order are: (1) Mom read a story, (2) Mom turned off the light, (3) Leo closed his eyes. The last thing was Leo closing his eyes.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'A boy named Finn was afraid of the dark. His dad gave him a small flashlight. Every night, Finn held the flashlight under his blanket and read books until he felt sleepy.' How did the flashlight help Finn? 🔦
options: It made the room brighter so he was no longer afraid of the dark
He used it to find his toys
He gave it to his dad
questions.explain: Finn used the flashlight to read under his blanket in the dark, which helped him feel less afraid because he had light and something to focus on.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'The wolf huffed and puffed. He blew down the house of straw. He blew down the house of sticks. But he could NOT blow down the house of bricks.' Which house did the wolf FAIL to blow down?
questions.explain: The passage states the wolf could NOT blow down the house of bricks. He succeeded with straw and sticks but failed with bricks.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Nina found a stray cat on her doorstep. She gave it milk and a warm bed. The next morning, the cat was still there, purring.' What did Nina most likely FEEL when she saw the cat still there? 🐱
options: Scared because the cat was still there
Happy because the cat seemed to want to stay
Angry because the cat drank the milk
Sad because she had to leave
questions.explain: Nina was kind to the cat and the cat stayed, purring. We can infer she felt happy because the cat showed it wanted to stay with her.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Omar loved to draw. He drew pictures of rockets, oceans, and dragons. His teacher put his drawings on the wall for everyone to see.' Who put Omar's drawings on the wall?
questions.explain: The passage says 'His teacher put his drawings on the wall for everyone to see.' The teacher is clearly stated as the one who displayed the artwork.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'The ugly duckling was sad because all the other ducks made fun of him. He swam away alone. In the spring, he looked in the water and saw a beautiful swan.' What is the main idea of this story? 🦢
options: Sometimes things that seem different turn out to be beautiful
questions.explain: The main idea is that the duckling who seemed different turned out to be a beautiful swan. The story teaches us not to judge by appearance — things that seem different can be wonderful.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Chloe got a new puppy. She named him Biscuit. She had to feed him, walk him, and play with him every day.' Why does Chloe have to do all those tasks? 🐾
options: Because the puppy told her to
Because taking care of a pet is the owner's responsibility
Because her teacher asked her to
questions.explain: Taking care of a pet — feeding, walking, and playing with it — is the responsibility of the owner. Chloe does these tasks because she is Biscuit's owner.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'The puppy was so tiny it could fit in my hand.' What does TINY mean? 🐶
questions.explain: The clue is that the puppy could fit in someone's hand. This tells us 'tiny' means very small.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which of these sentences is a QUESTION?
questions.explain: 'Can you tie your shoes?' is a question because it asks something and ends with a question mark. The others are statements.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word is a NOUN (a person, place, or thing)?
questions.explain: 'School' is a noun — it is a place. 'Jump' is a verb (action), 'happy' is an adjective (describing word), and 'quickly' is an adverb.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'She was so exhausted after the long hike that she fell asleep right away.' What does EXHAUSTED mean? 🥾
questions.explain: The context clue 'fell asleep right away' tells us she was very tired. 'Exhausted' means extremely tired.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word is a VERB (an action word) in the sentence: 'The rabbit hops through the meadow.'? 🐰
questions.explain: 'Hops' is the verb because it describes what the rabbit is doing — it is an action. 'Rabbit' and 'meadow' are nouns. 'Through' is a preposition.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which group of words are all FRUITS? 🍎🍌🍓
questions.explain: 'Mango,' 'grape,' and 'peach' are all fruits. The other options include vegetables (carrot, corn, lettuce, potato, celery) mixed with fruits.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'The baby giggled when her dad tickled her toes.' What does GIGGLED mean? 😄
options: laughed in a light, happy way
questions.explain: The context — being tickled and being a happy baby — tells us giggling is a light, happy kind of laughing. 'Giggled' means to laugh softly and cheerfully.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which of these is a STATEMENT (not a question)?
questions.explain: 'The flowers are pink.' is a statement because it tells us something and ends with a period. The other choices are all questions.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'The kitten was very timid. She hid under the couch every time someone new came into the house.' What does TIMID mean? 🐱
questions.explain: The clue is that the kitten hid when new people came. This shows she was shy and easily scared — the meaning of 'timid.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word does NOT belong in the category 'things you wear'? 👕
questions.explain: 'Hat,' 'socks,' and 'gloves' are all things you wear. A 'sandwich' is food — it does not belong in the category of clothing.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: In the sentence 'The brave firefighter climbed the tall ladder,' which word is a NOUN? 🚒
questions.explain: 'Firefighter' is a noun — it names a person. 'Brave' and 'tall' are adjectives (describing words), and 'climbed' is a verb (action word).

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'He was furious when his little brother broke his favorite toy.' What does FURIOUS mean? 😡
questions.explain: The context — his favorite toy was broken — tells us he felt strongly negative. 'Furious' means very angry.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which group of words are all ANIMALS? 🐘🐋🦁
questions.explain: 'Lion,' 'eagle,' and 'dolphin' are all animals. The other groups include plants (rose, oak, tulip) mixed in with animals.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word is a VERB (action word) in the sentence: 'The chef bakes delicious bread every morning.'? 🍞
questions.explain: 'Bakes' is the verb because it names what the chef is doing — an action. 'Chef' is a noun, 'delicious' is an adjective, and 'morning' is a noun.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'The ancient turtle moved very slowly across the sand.' What does ANCIENT most likely mean? 🐢
questions.explain: An 'ancient' turtle is one that is very old. Turtles are known for living a long time, and 'ancient' describes something extremely old.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 347 + 285?
questions.explain: 347 + 285: 7+5=12, write 2 carry 1; 4+8+1=13, write 3 carry 1; 3+2+1=6. Answer is 632.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 523 - 178?
questions.explain: 523 - 178: borrow to get 13-8=5; 1-7 needs borrowing: 11-7=4; 4-1=3. Answer is 345.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 468 + 354?
questions.explain: 468 + 354: 8+4=12, write 2 carry 1; 6+5+1=12, write 2 carry 1; 4+3+1=8. Answer is 822.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 700 - 263?
questions.explain: 700 - 263: borrowing across zeros gives 10-3=7; 9-6=3 (after borrowing); 6-2=4. Answer is 437.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What number makes this true? 254 + ___ = 600
questions.explain: 600 - 254 = 346. Check: 254 + 346 = 600. The missing addend is 346.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Rosa has 486 stickers. She gives away 197 stickers. How many stickers does Rosa have left?
questions.explain: 486 - 197: 6-7 needs borrowing: 16-7=9; 7-9 needs borrowing: 17-9=8; 3-1=2. Answer is 289.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Start at 530. Add 100 three times. What number do you get?

questions.subject: math
questions.explain: 275 + 138 = 413; then 413 + 46 = 459. The total of all three numbers is 459.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A school collected 362 cans on Monday and 479 cans on Tuesday. How many cans did the school collect in all?
questions.explain: 362 + 479: 2+9=11, write 1 carry 1; 6+7+1=14, write 4 carry 1; 3+4+1=8. Answer is 841.

questions.subject: math
questions.explain: 850 - 100 = 750; 750 - 100 = 650; 650 - 100 = 550. Subtracting 100 three times means subtracting 300: 850 - 300 = 550.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What number makes this true? ___ - 149 = 235

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: There are 605 books in the library. Students check out 278 books. How many books are still in the library?
questions.explain: 605 - 278: borrowing across the zero gives 15-8=7; 9-7=2 (after borrowing adjustments); 5-2=3. Answer is 327.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is the sum of 156, 234, and 87?
questions.explain: 156 + 234 = 390; 390 + 87 = 477. The sum of all three numbers is 477.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 999 - 456?
questions.explain: 999 - 456: 9-6=3; 9-5=4; 9-4=5. No borrowing needed. Answer is 543.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Jake had 500 baseball cards. He gave 163 to his friend and got 48 more. How many cards does Jake have now?
questions.explain: 500 - 163 = 337; then 337 + 48 = 385. Jake has 385 cards now.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which equation shows adding 10 to 479 mentally?
questions.explain: Adding 10 to any 3-digit number changes only the tens digit: 479 + 10 = 489.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 617 + 295?
questions.explain: 617 + 295: 7+5=12, write 2 carry 1; 1+9+1=11, write 1 carry 1; 6+2+1=9. Answer is 912.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: The farmer has 843 apples. He sells 376 apples. How many apples does he have left?
questions.explain: 843 - 376: 3-6 needs borrowing: 13-6=7; 3-7 needs borrowing: 13-7=6; 7-3=4. Answer is 467.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which pair of numbers adds up to exactly 1,000?

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Emma scored 248 points in a game. Ben scored 100 more points than Emma. How many points did Ben score?
questions.explain: 248 + 100 = 348. When adding 100, only the hundreds digit changes: 2 becomes 3. Ben scored 348 points.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 400 + ___ = 753? What is the missing number?
questions.explain: 753 - 400 = 353. The hundreds digit drops from 7 to 3 when subtracting 4 hundreds. The missing number is 353.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 732 - 465?
questions.explain: 732 - 465: 2-5 needs borrowing: 12-5=7; 2-6 needs borrowing: 12-6=6 (after adjusting); 6-4=2. Answer is 267.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Two classes collected cans. Room A collected 184 cans. Room B collected 237 cans. Room C collected 119 cans. How many cans in all?
questions.explain: 184 + 237 = 421; 421 + 119 = 540. The three classes collected 540 cans total.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 10 less than 803?
questions.explain: 803 - 10 = 793. When subtracting 10, only the tens digit changes: 0 becomes 9 with borrowing from hundreds. Answer is 793.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A store had 927 items. They sold 348 items on Saturday and 215 items on Sunday. How many items are left?

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is the value of the digit 7 in the number 573?
questions.explain: In 573, the digit 7 is in the tens place. The value of a digit in the tens place is the digit times 10: 7 x 10 = 70.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which number is the same as 600 + 40 + 9?
questions.explain: 600 is 6 hundreds, 40 is 4 tens, 9 is 9 ones. Written together: 649.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which symbol correctly compares 728 and 782?
questions.explain: Both have 7 hundreds. Compare tens: 2 tens < 8 tens. So 728 < 782.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is the expanded form of 805?
questions.explain: 805 in expanded form is 800 + 0 + 5: 8 hundreds, 0 tens, 5 ones. The other options name different numbers.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Skip-count by 100s starting at 47: 47, 147, 247, ___
questions.explain: When skip-counting by 100s, only the hundreds digit changes: 47, 147, 247, 347.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which number has a 4 in the hundreds place, a 0 in the tens place, and a 7 in the ones place?
questions.explain: 4 hundreds, 0 tens, 7 ones = 400 + 0 + 7 = 407.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is the largest 3-digit number you can make with the digits 3, 8, and 1?
questions.explain: To make the largest number, put the biggest digit in the hundreds place: 8, then 3, then 1. Answer: 831.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What number is 100 more than 689?
questions.explain: 100 more than 689: the hundreds digit increases by 1: 6+1=7. Answer is 789.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which shows the correct way to read 963?
questions.explain: 963 = 9 hundreds, 6 tens, 3 ones = nine hundred sixty-three.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Skip-count by 5s: 760, 765, 770, ___
questions.explain: Adding 5 each time: 760, 765, 770, 775.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which number is between 456 and 465?
questions.explain: 460 is greater than 456 and less than 465. Check: 456 < 460 < 465.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: How many tens are in 540?
questions.explain: 540 = 54 tens (5 hundreds = 50 tens, plus 4 tens). There are 54 tens in 540.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is the value of the underlined digit in 3_7_8? The digit 7 is underlined.
questions.explain: In 378, the 7 is in the tens place. Its value is 7 x 10 = 70.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which list shows numbers in order from least to greatest?
questions.explain: Comparing hundreds first: 298 (2 hundreds) < 389 (3 hundreds) < 398 (3 hundreds, 9 tens) < 839 (8 hundreds).

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What number equals 7 hundreds, 12 tens, and 3 ones?

questions.subject: math
questions.explain: Adding 10 each time: 640, 650, 660, 670.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which number, written in words, is 'five hundred four'?
questions.explain: Five hundred four = 500 + 4 = 504. There are no tens, so the tens digit is 0.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 100 less than 407?
questions.explain: 100 less than 407: the hundreds digit decreases by 1: 4-1=3. Answer is 307.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which of these is the same as 400 + 60 + 2?
questions.explain: 400 + 60 + 2 = 462. The digits go: 4 hundreds, 6 tens, 2 ones.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What number has the digit 9 in the hundreds place, digit 0 in the tens place, and digit 8 in the ones place?
questions.explain: 9 hundreds + 0 tens + 8 ones = 900 + 0 + 8 = 908.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: There are 36 red marbles and 47 blue marbles in a bag. Tim takes out 28 marbles. How many marbles are still in the bag?
questions.explain: 36 + 47 = 83 total marbles; 83 - 28 = 55 marbles remaining in the bag.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Is the number 47 odd or even? How do you know?
options: Odd, because 47 cannot be split into two equal groups
Odd, because it is greater than 40
questions.explain: 47 is odd because it ends in 7 (an odd digit) and cannot be split into two equal whole number groups.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Sara had some stickers. She gave 19 to her friend and now has 34 stickers left. How many stickers did Sara start with?
questions.explain: Sara started with 34 + 19 = 53 stickers. We add back the ones she gave away to find the start.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: There are 5 bags with 4 apples in each bag. Which equation shows the total number of apples?
questions.explain: 5 bags of 4 apples means adding 4 five times: 4+4+4+4+4 = 20. This is repeated addition for equal groups.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Max has 63 crayons. He buys 18 more and then breaks 9. How many unbroken crayons does Max have?
questions.explain: 63 + 18 = 81 crayons; 81 - 9 = 72 unbroken crayons.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which of these numbers is even?
questions.explain: 84 is even because it ends in 4, which is an even digit. It can be split into two equal groups of 42.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: The library had 85 books. They got a new shipment, and now have 100 books. Then they gave away 17 books. How many books does the library have now?
questions.explain: They started with 85, got 15 more to have 100, then gave away 17: 100 - 17 = 83.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: 3 children each have 6 toy cars. Which shows the total number of cars?
questions.explain: 3 groups of 6 means 6 + 6 + 6 = 18 cars total. Repeated addition of equal groups.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: There were 46 birds on a wire. 17 flew away. Then 23 more landed. How many birds are on the wire now?
questions.explain: 46 - 17 = 29 birds; 29 + 23 = 52 birds on the wire now.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Anna has 24 cookies. She wants to put them into groups of 3. How many groups will she have? Use repeated addition.
questions.explain: 3+3+3+3+3+3+3+3 = 24. She can make 8 groups of 3. Or 24 / 3 = 8 groups.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Kyle had 58 stamps. His sister had 29 fewer stamps than Kyle. How many stamps did Kyle's sister have?
questions.explain: 29 fewer means subtraction: 58 - 29 = 29. Kyle's sister had 29 stamps.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: 38 is an even number. Which of the following, when added to 38, will give an even sum?
questions.explain: 38 + 14 = 52, which is even. Even + even = even. 38 + 15 = 53 (odd), 38 + 23 = 61 (odd), 38 + 7 = 45 (odd). Only 14 gives an even sum.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Lena read 27 pages on Monday, 34 pages on Tuesday, and some pages on Wednesday. She read 90 pages total. How many pages did she read on Wednesday?
questions.explain: 27 + 34 = 61 pages on Mon and Tue. 90 - 61 = 29 pages on Wednesday.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: There are 4 rows of chairs with 7 chairs in each row. How many chairs are there in all?
questions.explain: 4 rows x 7 chairs = 7+7+7+7 = 28 chairs total. This is an equal groups problem.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: At the park, 33 kids are playing. 18 kids go home. Then 9 more kids arrive. How many kids are at the park now?
questions.explain: 33 - 18 = 15 kids; 15 + 9 = 24 kids at the park now.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Mia has 45 beads. Ben has 13 more beads than Mia. How many beads do they have together?
questions.explain: Ben has 45 + 13 = 58 beads. Together: 45 + 58 = 103 beads.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which best describes 36?
options: Even, because it ends in 6 but also has an odd digit
questions.explain: 36 is even because it can be split into two equal groups: 36 = 18 + 18. Even numbers are divisible by 2.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: There are 6 boxes with 5 pencils in each box. If you gave away 8 pencils, how many pencils would be left?
questions.explain: 6 boxes x 5 pencils = 5+5+5+5+5+5 = 30 pencils total; 30 - 8 = 22 pencils left.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: The pet store has 54 fish. They sell some fish and have 37 left. Then they get 15 new fish. How many fish are in the store now?
questions.explain: After selling: 37 fish. After getting 15 more: 37 + 15 = 52 fish.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Sam made 48 cookies. He ate some and had 39 left. How many cookies did Sam eat?
questions.explain: 48 - ? = 39, so ? = 48 - 39 = 9. Sam ate 9 cookies.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: 📏 A pencil is 17 centimeters long. A marker is 9 centimeters shorter than the pencil. How long is the marker?
questions.explain: 17 - 9 = 8. The marker is 8 centimeters long.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: 🕐 What time does the clock show if the hour hand points between 3 and 4, and the minute hand points to the 9?
questions.explain: The minute hand on the 9 means 45 minutes. The hour hand is between 3 and 4, so the hour is 3. Time: 3:45.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: 💰 You have 3 quarters, 2 dimes, and 1 nickel. How much money do you have in all?
questions.explain: 3 quarters = 75 cents; 2 dimes = 20 cents; 1 nickel = 5 cents; 75 + 20 + 5 = 100 cents = $1.00.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: 📏 A bookshelf is 36 inches long. A desk is 48 inches long. How much longer is the desk than the bookshelf?
questions.explain: 48 - 36 = 12 inches. The desk is 12 inches longer than the bookshelf.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A bar graph shows pets at the shelter: Dogs = 8, Cats = 12, Fish = 5, Birds = 7. How many more cats are there than fish and birds combined?
questions.explain: Fish + Birds = 5 + 7 = 12. Cats = 12. 12 - 12 = 0. There are the same number of cats as fish and birds combined — 0 more.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: 🕐 School starts at 8:00. Lunch is 2 hours and 30 minutes later. What time is lunch?

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: 💰 A toy costs $3.75. You pay with a $5 bill. How much change do you get?

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A book is 24 centimeters long. A pencil is 15 centimeters long. How much longer is the book than the pencil?
questions.explain: 24 − 15 = 9. The book is 9 centimeters longer than the pencil.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A picture graph shows favorite fruits. Apple = 4 stars, Banana = 6 stars, Grape = 3 stars. Each star = 2 students. How many students chose apple or banana?
questions.explain: Apple: 4 stars x 2 = 8 students; Banana: 6 stars x 2 = 12 students; 8 + 12 = 20 students chose apple or banana.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: 💰 Maya has 2 dollar bills, 3 quarters, and 4 pennies. How much money does Maya have?

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: 📏 A rope is 45 cm long. Another rope is 28 cm long. How long are both ropes together?
questions.explain: 45 + 28 = 73 cm. Together the two ropes are 73 centimeters long.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: 🕐 The movie started at 1:15. It lasted 1 hour and 30 minutes. What time did the movie end?
questions.explain: 1:15 + 1 hour = 2:15; 2:15 + 30 minutes = 2:45. The movie ended at 2:45.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A line plot shows the lengths of 5 worms: 3 cm, 5 cm, 3 cm, 7 cm, 5 cm. What is the difference between the longest and shortest worm?
questions.explain: Longest worm = 7 cm; shortest worm = 3 cm; 7 - 3 = 4 cm difference.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: 💰 A notebook costs $1.45 and a pen costs $0.80. How much do both items cost together?

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: 📏 Anna's arm is 18 inches long. Her leg is 32 inches long. How much longer is her leg than her arm?
questions.explain: 32 - 18 = 14 inches. Anna's leg is 14 inches longer than her arm.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A bar graph shows books read: Jan=9, Feb=7, Mar=11, Apr=6. Which month had the most books read? How many more books were read that month than in April?
questions.explain: March had the most with 11 books. 11 - 6 = 5 more books than April.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: 🕐 What time is 25 minutes after 7:20?

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: 💰 A snack costs $0.65. You have 2 quarters, 1 dime, and 3 nickels. Do you have enough, and how much money do you have in all?
options: Yes, you have $0.75 — that is 10 cents more than the cost
No, you have only $0.60 — 5 cents short
questions.explain: 2 quarters = 50c; 1 dime = 10c; 3 nickels = 15c; total = 75 cents. The snack costs 65 cents so you have enough — 10 cents more than needed.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: 📏 A caterpillar is 8 cm long. It grows 5 more centimeters. How long is the caterpillar now in millimeters? (1 cm = 10 mm)
questions.explain: 8 + 5 = 13 cm; 13 cm x 10 mm = 130 mm. The caterpillar is 130 millimeters long.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A number line goes from 0 to 100 by 10s. A frog is at 30. It jumps 25 units to the right. Where does the frog land?
questions.explain: 30 + 25 = 55. The frog lands on 55 on the number line.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A shape has 4 sides and 4 right angles, and all sides are equal. What shape is it?
questions.explain: A square has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles. A rectangle has 4 right angles but not all sides are equal.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A rectangle is divided into 3 equal rows and 4 equal columns. How many equal parts is it divided into?
questions.explain: 3 rows x 4 columns = 12 equal parts. Multiplying rows by columns gives the total number of equal pieces.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A pizza is cut into 4 equal pieces. One piece is eaten. What fraction of the pizza is left?
questions.explain: The pizza was cut into 4 equal pieces (fourths). 1 piece was eaten, so 3 pieces remain: 3/4 of the pizza is left.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which 3D shape has exactly 6 flat faces, all of which are squares?
questions.explain: A cube has 6 faces and all faces are equal squares. A rectangular prism also has 6 faces but they are not all squares.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A rectangle is cut into 2 equal parts. What is each part called?
questions.explain: When a shape is divided into 2 equal parts, each part is called a half. 1 out of 2 equal parts = 1/2.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: How many angles does a pentagon have?
questions.explain: A pentagon has 5 sides and 5 angles. The number of sides always equals the number of angles in a polygon.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A square is divided into 4 equal parts. Two parts are shaded. What fraction is shaded?
questions.explain: 2 out of 4 equal parts are shaded, so 2/4 is shaded. This is also equal to 1/2.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which 3D shape has 2 flat circular faces and 1 curved surface?
questions.explain: A cylinder has 2 circular flat faces (top and bottom) and 1 curved surface on the side.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A rectangle is divided into 2 rows and 5 columns. How many small squares are there? What is the area model?
questions.explain: 2 rows x 5 columns = 10 equal squares. The area model shows 2 x 5 = 10.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A circle is divided into 3 equal parts. One part is shaded. What fraction of the circle is shaded?
questions.explain: The circle is divided into 3 equal parts (thirds). 1 out of 3 parts is shaded, so 1/3 is shaded.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which shape has exactly 6 sides?
questions.explain: A hexagon has exactly 6 sides and 6 angles. Penta- = 5, Octa- = 8, Quadri- = 4.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A rectangle is divided into 4 equal rows and 3 equal columns. Toby colors 6 of the small rectangles. What fraction of the whole rectangle did Toby color?
questions.explain: 4 rows x 3 columns = 12 total parts. Toby colored 6 out of 12, so 6/12 of the rectangle (which equals 1/2).

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which statement about a cone is TRUE?
options: A cone has 1 flat face and 1 curved surface
questions.explain: A cone has 1 flat circular face (the base) and 1 curved surface that comes to a point.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Lisa cuts a sandwich into 4 equal pieces and eats 1 piece. Her brother eats 2 pieces. What fraction of the sandwich is left?
questions.explain: 4 total pieces; 1 + 2 = 3 eaten; 4 - 3 = 1 piece left; 1 out of 4 = 1/4 of the sandwich remains.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A rectangular garden is divided into 3 equal rows and 3 equal columns for planting. How many equal sections are there? If Maya plants tomatoes in 4 sections, what fraction of the garden has tomatoes?
questions.explain: 3 rows x 3 columns = 9 sections total. Maya plants tomatoes in 4 out of 9 sections, so 4/9 of the garden has tomatoes.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word uses a vowel team to make the long /e/ sound?
questions.explain: 'Steam' uses the vowel team 'ea' to make the long /e/ sound. The other words with 'ea' actually make a short /e/ sound.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word is spelled correctly using the CVCe pattern to make a long vowel sound?
questions.explain: 'Kite' follows the CVCe pattern (consonant-vowel-consonant-e) correctly, giving the 'i' a long /i/ sound.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: The word 'knight' has a silent letter combination. Which letters are silent?
questions.explain: In 'knight,' the 'kn' at the beginning and 'gh' in the middle are both silent. You only hear the /n/ and /t/ sounds.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which pair of words are homophones (sound the same but have different meanings)?
questions.explain: 'Write' and 'right' are homophones — they sound exactly the same but are spelled differently and have different meanings.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: What does the prefix 'un-' mean in the word 'unhappy'?
questions.explain: The prefix 'un-' means 'not.' So 'unhappy' means 'not happy.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: How many syllables are in the word 'umbrella'?
questions.explain: 'Umbrella' has 3 syllables: um-brel-la.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word has an r-controlled vowel that makes the /ar/ sound?
questions.explain: 'Cart' has the 'ar' pattern which makes the r-controlled /ar/ sound. The other words have r-controlled vowels but make different sounds (/er/).

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: What is the contraction for 'they are'?
questions.explain: 'They're' is the contraction for 'they are.' The apostrophe replaces the 'a' in 'are.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word uses the suffix '-ful' correctly?
questions.explain: 'Joyful' is spelled correctly with the suffix '-ful' (one l). It means 'full of joy.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: The word 'telephone' can be broken into syllables. Which is correct?
questions.explain: 'Telephone' breaks into 3 syllables: tel-e-phone. Each syllable has one vowel sound.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word contains a vowel team that makes the long /o/ sound?
questions.explain: 'Boat' contains the vowel team 'oa' which makes the long /o/ sound.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: What does the prefix 're-' mean in the word 'rewrite'?
questions.explain: The prefix 're-' means 'again.' So 'rewrite' means 'to write again.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word has the r-controlled vowel pattern 'ir' that makes the /er/ sound?
questions.explain: 'Bird' has the 'ir' r-controlled vowel that makes the /er/ sound.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the correct homophone?
questions.explain: The correct word is 'see,' meaning to look at something. 'Sea' is a body of water — a different homophone.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word uses the suffix '-less' to mean 'without fear'?
questions.explain: 'Fearless' uses the suffix '-less' which means 'without.' So 'fearless' means 'without fear.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: In the word 'explore,' what vowel sound does the letter 'e' at the end create in the first syllable?
options: The final 'e' is silent and has no effect here
questions.explain: In 'explore,' the final 'e' is silent. The word does not follow a simple CVCe pattern across syllables — the 'o' in '-plore' is controlled by the 'r.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word is a compound word?
questions.explain: 'Sunshine' is a compound word made of two smaller words: 'sun' and 'shine.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word uses the 'igh' spelling pattern for the long /i/ sound?
questions.explain: 'Light' uses the 'igh' spelling pattern to make the long /i/ sound.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: What does the contraction 'couldn't' stand for?
questions.explain: 'Couldn't' is the contraction for 'could not.' The apostrophe replaces the 'o' in 'not.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word has the 'or' r-controlled vowel making the /or/ sound?
questions.explain: 'Horn' has the 'or' r-controlled vowel making the clear /or/ sound. The other words have 'or' or 'wor' but make the /er/ sound.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Maya had practiced her dance for weeks. The night of the show, her knees shook and her hands felt cold. But when the music started, her feet seemed to remember every step. At the end, the whole audience clapped.' Why did Maya's feet 'seem to remember every step'?
options: She had practiced so much that her body knew what to do.
The music told her what to do.
Her teacher stood behind the curtain and helped her.
questions.explain: Maya had practiced for weeks, so through repetition her body knew the dance automatically even when she was nervous.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'The fox saw grapes hanging high on a vine. He jumped and jumped but could not reach them. Finally, he walked away saying, "Those grapes are probably sour anyway."' What does this fable teach?
options: It is smart to test food before eating it.
People sometimes pretend they do not want what they cannot have.
questions.explain: The fable teaches that people sometimes pretend something is not worth having when they cannot get it — this is the lesson 'sour grapes.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Leo never shared his crayons. One rainy day, Leo forgot his pencil. No one in class would lend him one. Leo sat staring at his blank paper.' What is the most likely reason no one lent Leo a pencil?
options: The other kids had no extra pencils.
The teacher said sharing was not allowed.
Leo had never been kind to others, so they did not want to help him.
questions.explain: Because Leo never shared, the other students likely felt no reason to help him. The story connects his behavior to the consequence he experienced.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'The old woman lived alone in the woods. Each morning she left bread crumbs on her porch. Birds and rabbits came every day. "I may be alone," she said quietly, "but I am never lonely."' What does the old woman mean?
options: She wishes she had human friends.
The animals keep her company so she does not feel sad.
She is too busy to feel anything.
questions.explain: The old woman means that even though no people live with her, the animals she feeds give her companionship, so she does not feel lonely.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Cinderella worked hard every day while her stepsisters played. When the prince invited everyone to the ball, her stepmother said Cinderella could not go. But a fairy godmother appeared and helped her get ready.' Who is the most important problem-solver in this part of the story?
questions.explain: In this section of the story, the fairy godmother is the one who solves Cinderella's problem by helping her go to the ball.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'The sun shines on the meadow, / Warming every blade of grass. / Bees hum their busy music, / As the slow summer hours pass.' What feeling does this poem most likely give the reader?
questions.explain: Words like 'warming,' 'slow,' and 'hum' create a calm, peaceful mood in this poem.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Tom ran ahead on the trail. His little sister Bea called out, "Wait!" Tom kept running. Then he heard a thud and a cry. He turned to find Bea on the ground with a twisted ankle. Tom wished he had listened.' What caused Bea to get hurt?
options: Tom ran ahead and did not wait for Bea, so she was alone when she fell.
Bea forgot to tie her shoes.
questions.explain: Tom did not wait for Bea, so she was left behind alone on the trail when she fell. Tom's choice not to listen caused the problem.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Rabbit always boasted about how fast he could run. Tortoise challenged him to a race. Rabbit raced ahead, then napped under a tree. Tortoise walked slowly and steadily. When Rabbit woke up, Tortoise had already crossed the finish line.' Compare Rabbit and Tortoise. What is the key difference in how they approached the race?
options: Rabbit had four legs and Tortoise had none.
Rabbit was overconfident and careless; Tortoise was steady and focused.
Rabbit was slower but tried harder.
Tortoise cheated by taking a shortcut.
questions.explain: Rabbit was overconfident and stopped to nap, while Tortoise stayed focused and kept going steadily. This difference explains why Tortoise won.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Lila found a baby bird on the sidewalk. She wanted to keep it, but her dad said, "We should call a wildlife rescue center. They know how to care for wild animals." Lila was disappointed, but she made the call. A few weeks later, the center sent her a photo: the bird was flying free.' Why did Lila's dad say to call the rescue center?
options: He did not want a bird in the house.
Experts at the center are better trained to care for wild animals.
It was against the law to touch birds.
The bird was too sick to survive.
questions.explain: Lila's dad knew the rescue center had the knowledge and skills to properly care for a wild bird, making it the best choice for the animal.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Prince Arlo was brave in battle but terrified of spiders. One night, a small spider spun a web in his window. Arlo screamed and called his guards. The guards tried not to smile.' What does the author want the reader to understand about Prince Arlo?
options: He is cruel to his guards.
Even brave people can have unexpected fears.
He is not really brave at all.
questions.explain: The author shows that a brave warrior can still be frightened by something small, suggesting that everyone has fears.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'First, Grandma stirred the batter. Next, she poured it into the pan. Then she slid it into the hot oven. Finally, the kitchen filled with the sweet smell of banana bread.' What happened right BEFORE the kitchen smelled sweet?
options: Grandma poured the batter into the pan.
Grandma slid the pan into the oven.
Grandma took the bread out of the oven.
questions.explain: According to the sequence, Grandma slid the pan into the oven right before the kitchen filled with the sweet smell.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Ana and her brother Dario both wanted the last orange. Ana said they should split it. But Dario wanted the peel to make a dessert, and Ana wanted the fruit inside. They laughed when they realized they each could take the part they needed.' What is the lesson of this story?
options: Talking about what you need can lead to a better solution than fighting.
questions.explain: By talking about what each of them actually wanted, Ana and Dario found a perfect solution. The lesson is that communication leads to better outcomes.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Mia hid her report card under her mattress. At dinner, her parents talked about how proud they were of her sister's grades. Mia pushed her peas around her plate and said nothing.' How is Mia most likely feeling?
questions.explain: Mia hid her report card and went quiet during dinner, suggesting she feels ashamed of her grades and worried about her parents finding out.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Jack climbed the beanstalk and found a castle in the clouds. Inside lived a giant who had stolen treasures from Jack's family long ago. Jack grabbed the golden harp and ran for the beanstalk.' Why did Jack take the golden harp?
options: He wanted to sell it at the market.
It had originally belonged to his family.
The giant told him to take it.
questions.explain: The passage states the giant had stolen treasures from Jack's family, so Jack was reclaiming what was rightfully his.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Crow was thirsty and found a pitcher with a little water at the bottom. Her beak could not reach it. Then she had an idea: she dropped pebbles into the pitcher, one by one. The water rose until she could drink.' What does this fable show about Crow?
options: Crows like to collect shiny things.
Crow solved a problem by thinking creatively.
Crow was lucky to find water.
Crow gave up when things got hard.
questions.explain: Crow used problem-solving and creative thinking — dropping pebbles to raise the water level — rather than giving up.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'The new kid stood alone at recess. Jada watched from near the swings. She remembered her first week at this school — how long the days had felt. She walked over and said, "Want to play?"' Why did Jada walk over to the new kid?
options: She felt bored and had nothing else to do.
She understood how lonely the new kid might feel because she had felt the same way.
The new kid looked like her old friend.
questions.explain: Jada remembered feeling lonely her first week and used that empathy to motivate herself to include the new kid.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Rain, rain, go away, / Come again another day. / Little children want to play, / Rain, rain, go away.' What type of writing is this?
questions.explain: This is a poem/nursery rhyme. It has a rhyme scheme and rhythm, and expresses a feeling rather than telling a story with characters.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Sara loved to paint. One day her little brother knocked over her paints. Sara yelled at him. He started to cry. Sara felt her anger melt away. She handed him a clean brush and said, "Let's paint together."' What changed Sara's mood?
options: She saw her brother cry and felt sorry for him.
Her mother told her to calm down.
She realized the paints were not ruined.
questions.explain: Sara's anger melted when she saw her brother cry, showing her empathy took over and she chose kindness instead.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Goldilocks tried Papa Bear's porridge — too hot. She tried Mama Bear's — too cold. She tried Baby Bear's — just right. She ate it all up.' Which word best describes Goldilocks based on her actions?
questions.explain: Goldilocks tries everything until she finds what she wants and takes it all, showing she is picky and does not think about others.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Two friends, Dev and Sam, both wanted to be team captain. Dev thought he deserved it because he was the fastest runner. Sam thought she deserved it because she always made sure everyone played.' Compare Dev and Sam's reasons for wanting to be captain.
options: Dev focused on personal skill; Sam focused on helping the team.
Dev and Sam both wanted to win for their team.
Sam was faster so she should be captain.
Dev was the better leader because he ran fast.
questions.explain: Dev's reason was his individual speed, while Sam's reason was her teamwork and care for others — these are different leadership styles.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'The little engine huffed up the hill carrying toys for children on the other side. "I think I can, I think I can," it repeated. At last it reached the top and rolled down, shouting, "I knew I could!"' What does the phrase 'I think I can' tell you about the engine?
options: The engine was not sure it could do it but kept trying.
The engine was certain it would succeed.
The engine was asking for help.
The engine was bragging about its strength.
questions.explain: 'I think I can' (not 'I know I can') shows the engine had some doubt but chose to believe in itself and keep going despite uncertainty.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Every night, Marco looked at the same star from his window. He imagined it blinking just for him. The star seemed close, like a friend. When clouds covered the sky, Marco felt a little lonely.' What does the star represent for Marco?
options: A source of comfort and friendship
questions.explain: Marco treats the star like a friend, feels connected to it, and feels lonely without it — it represents comfort and companionship.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'The three billy goats wanted to cross the bridge to eat green grass. But a mean troll lived under the bridge. The smallest goat went first, then the middle goat, and finally the biggest goat knocked the troll off the bridge.' What is the most likely reason the goats went in order from smallest to biggest?
options: The smallest goat was the bravest.
They planned it so the biggest and strongest goat could defeat the troll.
The troll only feared small goats.
They drew straws to decide the order.
questions.explain: The goats sent the smaller ones first with promises of a bigger goat to come, saving the biggest and strongest goat to finally defeat the troll — it was a strategy.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Zara loved her old, worn stuffed bear. Her aunt gave her a shiny new toy robot for her birthday. Zara smiled and said thank you. But that night, she tucked the bear in beside her as always.' What does Zara's action at night tell you?
options: She did not like the robot.
The bear meant more to her than the new toy.
Her aunt told her to keep the bear.
questions.explain: Even with a shiny new toy, Zara chose her old bear at bedtime, showing its sentimental value meant more to her.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'When the wolf blew down the straw house, the pig ran to his brother's stick house. The wolf blew that down too. Both pigs ran to the brick house. The wolf huffed and puffed but could not blow it down.' What does this story show about the importance of being prepared?
options: Taking time to do things carefully and well pays off in the end.
Three pigs are better than one.
questions.explain: The third pig who built with bricks took more time and effort to prepare, and that preparation protected all three pigs — it shows that doing things well matters.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Wolves live in groups called packs. They hunt together and care for their young. A mother wolf is called a she-wolf. The leader of the pack is the alpha.' Wait — this passage sounds different from a story. What kind of text is this?
questions.explain: This text gives facts about wolves (group name, behavior, vocabulary) without a plot or characters — that makes it informational nonfiction.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Penny found a $10 bill on the sidewalk. She could buy anything she wanted! She looked around. A little girl nearby was crying — she had dropped her ice cream. Penny bought the girl a new one and walked home with empty pockets but a big smile.' What does Penny's smile at the end suggest?
options: Helping someone else made her happy.
The ice cream was very good.
She was relieved to go home.
questions.explain: Penny gave away her money to help someone else and walked home smiling — this shows that acts of kindness bring their own reward: happiness.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'There once was a girl who planted a seed. She watered it every day, even when she was tired, even in the rain. One spring morning, she found a tall sunflower growing in her garden.' What is the theme of this short story?
options: Consistent effort and patience lead to results.
questions.explain: The story shows that the girl's daily, persistent care — even when it was hard — resulted in a beautiful sunflower. The theme is that steady effort pays off.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'The knight rode into the dark forest alone. Strange sounds came from every direction. His horse whinnied and danced sideways. The knight's heart beat fast, but he kept his sword ready and pushed forward.' Which words show that the knight was afraid but brave?
options: 'his heart beat fast, but he kept his sword ready and pushed forward'
questions.explain: 'His heart beat fast' shows fear, while 'kept his sword ready and pushed forward' shows bravery. Together they show he was afraid but acted bravely.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Gus always said he hated reading. Then his class visited the library, and he found a book about sharks. He read the whole thing in one afternoon. At dinner, he talked about nothing else.' What most likely changed Gus's feeling about reading?
options: His teacher made him read the shark book.
He found a topic he was genuinely interested in.
He wanted to impress his parents.
The library had no other books.
questions.explain: Gus discovered a book about something he loved — sharks — and that passion made reading enjoyable. Finding a personal interest is what changed his attitude.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Bees are important pollinators. When a bee lands on a flower to drink nectar, pollen sticks to its fuzzy body. When the bee visits the next flower, pollen rubs off and fertilizes it. Without bees, many plants could not make seeds or fruit.' What is the MAIN idea of this passage?
options: Bees are essential for plants to reproduce.
questions.explain: The main idea is that bees play a crucial role in plant reproduction (pollination). The other details support this main idea.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Ruby Bridges was six years old when she became the first Black child to attend William Frantz Elementary School in New Orleans in 1960. She walked through angry crowds every day with federal marshals protecting her. She showed incredible courage.' Which detail BEST supports the idea that Ruby Bridges was courageous?
options: She went to William Frantz Elementary School.
She walked through angry crowds every day.
questions.explain: Walking through angry crowds every day, despite the fear and hostility, is the detail that best shows her personal courage.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'The water cycle has four main steps. First, the sun heats water in oceans and lakes, causing it to evaporate. Then the water vapor rises and cools, forming clouds in a step called condensation. Next, the water falls as rain or snow in a step called precipitation. Finally, it collects in rivers and lakes again.' What text structure does this passage use?
questions.explain: The passage uses a sequence structure, describing the steps of the water cycle in order using words like 'first,' 'then,' 'next,' and 'finally.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Sharks have been on Earth for about 450 million years — long before dinosaurs. Their skeletons are made of cartilage, not bone. Sharks must keep swimming to breathe because water must flow over their gills.' In this passage, what does the word 'cartilage' most likely mean?
options: A flexible material that makes up the skeleton instead of hard bone
The sharp teeth of a shark
The skin that covers a shark
questions.explain: The passage contrasts cartilage with bone ('not bone'), telling us cartilage is a different skeletal material. It is flexible and lighter than bone.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Harriet Tubman was born into slavery but escaped to freedom in 1849. She then risked her life returning to the South more than a dozen times to help other enslaved people escape using the Underground Railroad, a secret network of safe houses.' Why did Harriet Tubman keep returning to the South after she was already free?
options: She forgot something when she left.
She wanted to help others gain their freedom, even at great personal risk.
She worked as a guide for money.
The Underground Railroad required her to return.
questions.explain: The passage states she 'risked her life' returning to help others escape, showing she put others' freedom above her own safety.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Recycling helps reduce waste in landfills. When we recycle paper, fewer trees are cut down. Recycling aluminum cans saves energy. Every small action adds up to make a big difference for our planet.' What is the author's purpose in writing this passage?
options: To entertain readers with a funny story about trash
To persuade readers that recycling is important and beneficial
To explain exactly how recycling machines work
To compare different types of garbage
questions.explain: The author lists benefits of recycling and ends with an encouraging statement, showing the purpose is to persuade readers that recycling matters.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Frogs are amphibians. They begin life as eggs in water. When eggs hatch, tadpoles emerge with tails and gills. Over time, tadpoles grow legs and lungs, losing their tails. Finally, they become adult frogs that can live both on land and in water.' Which detail is a supporting detail, NOT the main idea?
options: Frogs change form as they grow from egg to adult.
Frogs can live on land and in water.
questions.explain: 'Tadpoles have tails and gills' is a supporting detail that describes one stage of the frog's life cycle, not the overall main idea.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'The Amazon Rainforest covers much of South America. It is home to millions of species of plants and animals. The forest produces oxygen and absorbs carbon dioxide. Many scientists call it the lungs of the Earth.' Why do scientists call the Amazon Rainforest 'the lungs of the Earth'?
options: It is shaped like a pair of lungs on a map.
Like lungs, it takes in carbon dioxide and releases oxygen for the Earth.
questions.explain: Lungs take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide. The Amazon does the reverse — taking in CO2 and producing oxygen — making it like Earth's lungs for the planet.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Martin Luther King Jr. led peaceful marches and gave powerful speeches to fight for equal rights for all Americans. He believed that nonviolent protest was the most powerful tool for change. His work helped lead to the Civil Rights Act of 1964.' What does the word 'nonviolent' mean in this passage?
options: Protesting without using violence or fighting
questions.explain: The prefix 'non-' means 'not,' so 'nonviolent' means 'not violent' — protesting peacefully without fighting or using force.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Monarch butterflies travel up to 3,000 miles from Canada to Mexico each fall. No single butterfly makes the full round trip. It takes several generations to complete the journey. Scientists still study how they find their way.' What is most surprising about the monarch butterfly migration?
options: No single butterfly completes the whole trip — it takes multiple generations.
questions.explain: The most surprising fact is that no single butterfly lives long enough to complete the full journey — multiple generations work together over thousands of miles.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Dolphins are mammals, not fish. They breathe air through a blowhole on top of their heads. Dolphins are very intelligent and communicate with clicks and whistles. They live in groups called pods.' Compare dolphins and fish. What is one way they are DIFFERENT according to the passage?
options: Dolphins live in water; fish do not.
Dolphins breathe air; fish breathe underwater through gills.
Dolphins eat fish but fish do not eat dolphins.
questions.explain: The passage states dolphins breathe air through a blowhole, unlike fish which breathe underwater. This is a key difference mentioned in the text.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'In 1969, Neil Armstrong became the first person to walk on the Moon. He said the famous words: "That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind." The mission showed that humans could travel beyond Earth.' Why were Armstrong's words called a 'giant leap for mankind'?
options: He jumped very high on the Moon.
It meant all of humanity had achieved something historic and extraordinary.
The Moon mission took a long time.
questions.explain: Armstrong used 'giant leap for mankind' to mean it was a huge achievement for all of humanity — not just one person's step, but a historic milestone for the entire human race.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'The Sahara Desert is the world's largest hot desert. It gets less than 3 inches of rain each year. Despite this, many animals like camels, scorpions, and fennec foxes live there. These animals have special adaptations to survive the extreme heat and dryness.' What does the word 'adaptations' mean in this passage?
options: Special features that help animals survive in their environment
The tracks animals leave in sand
questions.explain: The passage says animals 'have special adaptations to survive the extreme heat and dryness,' meaning adaptations are features or traits that help them live in harsh conditions.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Community helpers keep our neighborhoods safe and healthy. Police officers patrol streets and respond to emergencies. Firefighters put out fires and rescue people. Doctors and nurses treat sick people. Each person's work helps others.' Which statement is a MAIN IDEA, not a detail?
options: Community helpers work together to keep people safe and healthy.
questions.explain: The statement about community helpers working together is the broad main idea. The other options are specific supporting details about individual helpers.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Trees give us oxygen to breathe. Their roots hold soil in place so it does not wash away in rain. They provide shelter and food for birds and insects. Planting trees is one of the best things people can do for the environment.' The author includes so many benefits of trees in order to —
options: prove that trees are the only important plants
convince readers that trees are valuable and worth protecting
show that animals depend only on trees
questions.explain: By listing multiple benefits, the author builds a strong case for why trees matter, with the goal of convincing readers to value and protect them.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Volcanoes can be found on land and under the sea. When a volcano erupts, melted rock called lava flows out. The lava cools and hardens, sometimes forming new land. The Hawaiian Islands were formed by underwater volcanoes.' What CAUSED the Hawaiian Islands to form?
options: Heavy rainfall carved out the islands.
Underwater volcanoes erupted and the lava cooled and built up land.
Earthquakes pushed land above the water.
Strong ocean waves shaped the islands.
questions.explain: The passage directly states the Hawaiian Islands were formed by underwater volcanoes — their lava cooled and hardened over time, building up land above the ocean surface.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Long ago, people got news by reading printed newspapers. Then came radio, followed by television. Today, most people get news instantly from websites and social media on their phones.' What text structure does this passage use?
questions.explain: The passage describes how news media changed over time, moving from newspapers to radio to TV to digital — this is a sequence/chronological text structure.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Penguins cannot fly, but they are excellent swimmers. Their wings have evolved into flippers perfect for cutting through water. Emperor penguins can dive over 1,800 feet deep and hold their breath for 20 minutes.' Which conclusion can you draw from this passage?
options: Penguins would be better animals if they could fly.
Penguins are well adapted to hunting fish in the ocean.
All birds that cannot fly are good swimmers.
questions.explain: Their flipper wings, deep diving ability, and long breath-holding are all adaptations that make penguins very effective ocean hunters.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Amelia Earhart was the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean, in 1932. She faced many challenges including stormy weather and mechanical problems. She said she flew not for fame, but because she loved the freedom of flight.' What motivated Amelia Earhart to fly?
options: She was paid a large sum of money.
She loved the freedom that flying gave her.
She wanted to prove women were better pilots than men.
questions.explain: The passage directly states Earhart said she flew 'because she loved the freedom of flight,' not for fame.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Soil is made up of tiny bits of rock, minerals, water, air, and decayed plants and animals. Earthworms help by tunneling through soil, which lets air and water in. Healthy soil is dark and rich.' How do earthworms help soil according to the passage?
options: They add minerals to the soil.
Their tunnels let air and water into the soil.
They make soil darker in color.
questions.explain: The passage states earthworms tunnel through soil, and this lets air and water in — improving soil health.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'The first subway in New York City opened in 1904. Before subways, people traveled by horse-drawn carriages or walked. Subways allowed millions of people to move quickly across the crowded city.' What problem did the subway SOLVE according to this passage?
options: People had no way to get to work.
It was slow and difficult to travel across the crowded city before the subway.
Horses were too expensive to own.
People did not want to walk anymore.
questions.explain: The passage shows that before the subway, travel was slow (horses, walking). The subway solved the problem of slow movement through a crowded city.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'The sun is a star at the center of our solar system. It is so large that about one million Earths could fit inside it. The sun provides the light and heat that make life on Earth possible.' Which sentence states a SUPPORTING DETAIL?
options: The sun is at the center of our solar system.
The sun provides the light and heat that make life on Earth possible.
About one million Earths could fit inside the sun.
The sun is the most important thing for life.
questions.explain: 'About one million Earths could fit inside the sun' is a specific fact (supporting detail) that supports the bigger idea that the sun is enormous.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Plants need sunlight, water, and nutrients from soil to grow. If a plant does not get enough sunlight, its leaves turn pale yellow. If it does not get enough water, it wilts and droops.' What would most likely happen to a plant kept in a dark closet?
options: It would grow faster without distractions.
Its leaves would turn pale yellow because it gets no sunlight.
questions.explain: The passage states that plants without enough sunlight turn pale yellow. A dark closet provides no sunlight, so this outcome is directly supported by the text.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'Ancient Egyptians built pyramids as tombs for their pharaohs. Workers used simple tools and ramps to move enormous stone blocks. The Great Pyramid at Giza was completed around 2560 BCE and is still one of the most remarkable structures ever built.' What can you infer about the workers who built the pyramids?
options: They used modern machines to move the stones.
They must have been highly skilled and extremely hardworking.
The pyramids were built very quickly in just a few years.
questions.explain: Moving enormous stone blocks with only simple tools requires incredible skill and hard work — we can infer this from what the passage describes.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'In autumn, many trees lose their leaves. Before leaves fall, they stop making chlorophyll, the green pigment. This lets other colors — yellow, orange, and red — show through. The colorful leaves then dry out and fall to the ground.' What CAUSES leaves to change color in autumn?
options: Trees stop making chlorophyll, allowing other colors to show.
Rain washes away the green color.
Animals eat the green parts of leaves.
questions.explain: The passage explains that when trees stop producing chlorophyll (green pigment), the yellow, orange, and red colors that were always there are revealed.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a collective noun correctly?
options: A flocks of birds flew over our heads.
A flock of birds flew over our heads.
Birds flocks flew over our heads.
questions.explain: 'A flock of birds' uses the collective noun 'flock' correctly to refer to a group of birds.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word is the correct irregular plural of 'goose'?
questions.explain: The irregular plural of 'goose' is 'geese.' It changes the vowel sound rather than adding -s.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a reflexive pronoun correctly?
options: She made the cake by herself.
She made the cake by herself own.
She made the cake by she.
questions.explain: 'By herself' correctly uses the reflexive pronoun 'herself,' showing she did it alone without help.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence is a compound sentence?
options: The dog barked, and the cat ran away.
questions.explain: 'The dog barked, and the cat ran away' is a compound sentence — it joins two complete sentences with the conjunction 'and.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses commas in a series correctly?
options: I need apples oranges and bananas.
I need apples, oranges, and bananas.
I need, apples, oranges and bananas.
I need apples, oranges and, bananas.
questions.explain: Commas in a series separate each item. 'I need apples, oranges, and bananas' correctly places commas after each item before the conjunction 'and.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses an apostrophe correctly to show possession?
questions.explain: 'The dog's bowl' correctly uses an apostrophe before the 's' to show that the bowl belongs to one dog.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses an adjective correctly to compare two things?
options: This book is more thicker than that one.
This book is thicker than that one.
This book is the thickest than that one.
This book is thick more than that one.
questions.explain: When comparing two things, use the '-er' comparative form: 'thicker.' Do not add 'more' when using '-er.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses an irregular plural noun correctly?
questions.explain: 'Children' is the correct irregular plural of 'child.' It does not follow the standard -s or -es pattern.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt:
Which word correctly completes the sentence? 'The boys cleaned the classroom _____.'
A: themselves
B: theirself
C: theirselves
D: themself
