questions.explain: The sentence uses a simile ('like a thunderbolt') to compare the sudden impact of the news to a lightning strike. This suggests Marco was powerfully surprised — the news hit him suddenly and intensely.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the word 'spring' as a VERB meaning to jump?
options: Spring is my favorite season because of the flowers.
Water flows from the mountain spring into the valley.
The cat will spring onto the counter if you leave food there.
She wore a light spring jacket on the cool morning.
questions.explain: In 'The cat will spring onto the counter,' 'spring' is a verb meaning to leap or jump. In the other sentences it functions as a noun (season, water source) or adjective.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word in the sentence is an ABSTRACT noun? 'Her courage inspired everyone on the team.'
questions.explain: 'Courage' is an abstract noun — it names a quality or idea that cannot be seen or touched. 'Team' is a concrete noun (a group of people you can observe).

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses an IRREGULAR verb correctly?
options: Yesterday she buyed a new book at the library.
He goed to the park after school on Friday.
They brought sandwiches to the picnic.
She taked the first bus to school this morning.
questions.explain: 'Brought' is the correct past tense of 'bring' — an irregular verb that does not follow the standard -ed pattern. 'Buyed,' 'goed,' and 'taked' are all incorrect past-tense forms.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a COMPARATIVE adjective correctly?
options: That mountain is more taller than the hill.
This puzzle is difficultier than the last one.
Today's weather is colder than yesterday's.
She is more smarter than her brother.
questions.explain: 'Colder' is the correct comparative form of 'cold' — add -er for short adjectives. 'More taller,' 'difficultier,' and 'more smarter' all incorrectly double the comparison.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which conjunction BEST completes this sentence? 'I wanted to go to the party, _____ I had too much homework to finish.'
questions.explain: 'But' is a coordinating conjunction showing contrast — the speaker wanted to go but was prevented by homework. 'And' adds information, 'or' presents a choice, and 'so' shows a result.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence is punctuated CORRECTLY with a comma after the introductory element?
options: After the long rain the streets were flooded.
After the long rain, the streets were flooded.
After, the long rain the streets were flooded.
After the long rain the streets, were flooded.
questions.explain: A comma is placed after an introductory phrase — in this case after 'After the long rain' — before the main clause. Option B places the comma in the correct position.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses quotation marks CORRECTLY in dialogue?
options: Marcus said, I can't believe we won!
"Marcus said, I can't believe we won!"
Marcus said, "I can't believe we won!"
Marcus said "I can't believe we won!"
questions.explain: Quotation marks enclose the exact words spoken and a comma separates the dialogue tag from the quote. 'Marcus said, "I can't believe we won!"' follows both rules correctly.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses 'because' correctly as a conjunction?
options: She stayed inside, because was raining.
Because she stayed inside the rain stopped.
She stayed inside because it was raining.
She stayed inside, because, it was raining.
questions.explain: 'Because' introduces a subordinate clause ('because it was raining') that explains the reason. No comma is needed before 'because' when it connects the main and subordinate clause in this order.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence is a COMPLEX sentence (contains one independent and one dependent clause)?
options: The dog barked and the cat ran away.
She studied hard, so she passed the test.
When the bell rang, the students rushed outside.
I like pizza and I like pasta.
questions.explain: 'When the bell rang' is a dependent clause (it cannot stand alone); 'the students rushed outside' is the independent clause. Together they form a complex sentence. Options A, B, and D are compound sentences.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses a comparative ADVERB?
options: She runs more faster than her sister.
He finished the test more quicker than anyone else.
The turtle moved more slowly than the rabbit.
They arrived more sooner than expected.
questions.explain: 'More slowly' is the correct comparative adverb form of 'slowly.' Options A, B, and D incorrectly double the comparison ('more faster,' 'more quicker,' 'more sooner').

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word is an ABSTRACT noun in this sentence? 'The children showed great kindness to the new student.'
questions.explain: 'Kindness' names a quality or feeling that cannot be physically touched or seen — it is an abstract noun. 'Children' and 'student' are concrete nouns.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses commas CORRECTLY in a list?
options: We need eggs milk, butter and flour for the recipe.
We need eggs, milk, butter, and flour for the recipe.
We need, eggs, milk, butter and flour for the recipe.
We need eggs milk butter and flour for the recipe.
questions.explain: Items in a series are separated by commas. 'We need eggs, milk, butter, and flour' correctly places a comma after each item (including before the final 'and').

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the conjunction 'so' correctly?
options: It was raining, so we brought umbrellas.
It was raining so but we forgot umbrellas.
So it was raining we brought umbrellas.
We brought umbrellas, so because it rained.
questions.explain: 'So' is a coordinating conjunction showing result or consequence. 'It was raining, so we brought umbrellas' correctly shows the cause (rain) and result (umbrellas). The other options use 'so' incorrectly.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly punctuates dialogue with the tag AFTER the spoken words?
questions.explain: When a dialogue tag follows spoken words, a comma (not a period) is placed inside the closing quotation mark, and the dialogue tag begins with a lowercase letter. Option B follows both rules.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the PAST TENSE of an irregular verb correctly?
options: Last night, she drawed a picture of her dog.
Last night, she drew a picture of her dog.
Last night, she drewed a picture of her dog.
Last night, she has drew a picture of her dog.
questions.explain: 'Drew' is the correct simple past tense of the irregular verb 'draw.' 'Drawed' and 'drewed' are incorrect; 'has drew' misuses the past participle.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the conjunction 'or' correctly to show a CHOICE?
options: You can have cake or you can have pie.
She studied hard or she passed the test.
He was tired or he fell asleep.
They played outside or it rained.
questions.explain: 'Or' presents two alternatives or choices. 'You can have cake or you can have pie' correctly offers two options. The other sentences use 'or' incorrectly — the clauses they join are causes/effects, not choices.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word is spelled correctly when you add the suffix -ING using the rule: drop the final e before adding a vowel suffix?
questions.explain: The word 'bake' ends in a silent e. When adding the vowel suffix -ing, the rule is to drop the e: bake → baking. 'Bakeing' keeps the e (incorrect); 'bakking' incorrectly doubles the k.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word is spelled correctly when you add -ING using the rule: double the final consonant when the word has a short vowel and ends in one consonant?
questions.explain: 'Run' has a short vowel (u) and ends in one consonant (n). The rule says to double the final consonant before adding -ing: run → running. 'Runing' breaks the rule; 'runeing' is nonsensical.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: How many syllables does the word 'comfortable' have?
questions.explain: 'Comfortable' is typically pronounced as four syllables in American English: com-for-ta-ble. Counting syllables by the number of vowel sounds heard gives four.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word correctly changes the adjective 'happy' into a NOUN using a suffix?
questions.explain: Adding the suffix -ness to an adjective forms a noun: happy → happiness. 'Happily' adds -ly (adverb), 'happier' adds -er (comparative adjective), and 'unhappy' adds the prefix un- (still an adjective).

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word has the long vowel sound in the STRESSED syllable? (The stressed syllable is underlined: pa-RADE)
questions.explain: In 'polite,' the stressed syllable is -LITE, which contains the long i sound (like 'kite'). In 'basket,' 'garden,' and 'happen,' the vowels in their stressed syllables are short.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which pair of words contains a word with the vowel pattern -igh- that makes the long i sound?
questions.explain: The vowel pattern -igh- always makes the long i sound. 'Night/fright,' 'light/fight,' and 'sight/might' all use this pattern correctly — so all of the above is correct.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word uses the suffix -FUL to change a noun into an adjective meaning 'full of'?
questions.explain: 'Fearful' (fear + -ful = full of fear), 'careful' (care + -ful = full of care), and 'painful' (pain + -ful = full of pain) all use -ful to turn a noun into an adjective. 'All of the above' is correct.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word correctly adds the suffix -ED using the doubling rule (short vowel + single consonant = double the consonant)?
questions.explain: 'Skip' has a short vowel (i) and ends in one consonant (p). The doubling rule says to double the p before adding -ed: skip → skipped. 'Skiped' breaks the rule by not doubling.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word correctly divides into syllables at the correct boundary for a VCCV pattern (vowel-consonant-consonant-vowel)?
questions.explain: In a VCCV pattern, the syllable boundary falls between the two consonants: nap-kin. The first syllable is closed (short vowel), and the word divides neatly between p and k.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which suffix changes the verb 'teach' into a NOUN meaning 'a person who teaches'?
questions.explain: The suffix -er added to a verb creates an agent noun meaning 'a person who does that action.' teach + -er = teacher, meaning a person who teaches. The other suffixes do not form agent nouns.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What number comes after 9 when you count?
questions.explain: When we count 1, 2, 3 … 9, the next number is 10.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: You are counting by 10s: 10, 20, 30, ___. What comes next?
questions.explain: When we count by 10s, after 30 comes 40.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Start at 6 and count forward three numbers. What number do you land on?
questions.explain: Starting at 6 and counting 7, 8, 9 — we land on 9.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Count forward from 14: 14, 15, ___. What is the missing number?
questions.explain: Counting forward, after 14 and 15 comes 16.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which number shows fifteen?
questions.explain: Fifteen is written as 15 — a 1 and a 5 together.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A teacher writes the number that comes after nineteen on the board. Which number did she write?
questions.explain: The number that comes after 19 is 20.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: How many apples are shown? 🍎🍎🍎🍎
questions.explain: Count each apple: 1, 2, 3, 4 — there are 4 apples.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A jar has 7 cookies. Which group shows exactly 7 items?
questions.explain: Seven cookies is shown by the group with exactly 7 cookie symbols.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: How many stars are there? ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
questions.explain: Count the stars one by one: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 — there are 7 stars.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Count the balloons: 🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈. How many are there?
questions.explain: Count each balloon: there are 12 balloons in all.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: There are 3 dogs 🐶🐶🐶 and 5 cats 🐱🐱🐱🐱🐱. Which group has MORE?
questions.explain: 5 cats is more than 3 dogs, so the cats group has more.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Sara has 6 crayons and Ben has 6 crayons. Which statement is true?
questions.explain: Both Sara and Ben have 6 crayons, so they have equal amounts.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which number is greater: 4 or 9?
questions.explain: 9 is greater than 4 because 9 comes later when we count.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which number is less: 12 or 7?
questions.explain: 7 is less than 12 because 7 comes before 12 when we count.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: There are 4 birds in a tree. 3 more birds fly in. How many birds are there now?
questions.explain: 4 birds plus 3 more birds equals 7 birds in all.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: There are 8 fish in a bowl. 3 fish swim away. How many fish are left?
questions.explain: 8 fish minus 3 fish that swam away leaves 5 fish.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 3 + 4?
questions.explain: 3 plus 4 equals 7.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 9 − 4?
questions.explain: 9 minus 4 equals 5.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which two numbers add up to 7?
questions.explain: 3 plus 4 equals 7, so 7 can be broken into 3 and 4.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Anna has 6 stickers. She puts some on her notebook and the rest on her folder. She puts 2 on her notebook. How many does she put on her folder?
questions.explain: 6 minus 2 equals 4, so she puts 4 stickers on her folder.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What number do you add to 6 to make 10?
questions.explain: 6 plus 4 equals 10, so you need to add 4.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: There are 7 frogs on a log. How many more frogs need to jump on to make 10 frogs?
questions.explain: 7 plus 3 equals 10, so 3 more frogs need to jump on.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 2 + 3?
questions.explain: 2 plus 3 equals 5.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 5 − 2?
questions.explain: 5 minus 2 equals 3.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: The number 13 means one ten and how many ones?
questions.explain: 13 is made of one group of ten and 3 leftover ones.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: One ten and 7 ones make which number?
questions.explain: One ten (10) plus 7 ones equals 17.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which word describes how long something is?
questions.explain: Length describes how long or short something is.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A bucket full of sand is HEAVY. What measurable attribute describes this?
questions.explain: Weight tells us how heavy or light something is.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A giraffe is taller than a rabbit. Which animal is SHORTER?
questions.explain: The rabbit is shorter because the giraffe is taller.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Book A is heavier than Book B. Which book is LIGHTER?
questions.explain: Book B is lighter because Book A is heavier.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A teacher sorts these shapes: 3 squares, 2 triangles, and 1 circle. How many circles are there?
questions.explain: There is only 1 circle in the group.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: In a bag there are 4 red blocks and 3 blue blocks. Which color has MORE blocks?
questions.explain: There are 4 red blocks and only 3 blue blocks, so red has more.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: The cat is sitting on TOP of the box. Which position word describes this?
questions.explain: When something is on top of something else, we say it is above it.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: The ball is NEXT TO the chair. Which position word means the same thing?
questions.explain: Next to means beside — the ball is beside the chair.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: This shape has 3 sides and 3 corners. What is it called?
questions.explain: A triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which shape has 6 sides?
questions.explain: A hexagon has 6 sides.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A soccer ball is a sphere. Is a sphere a flat (2D) shape or a solid (3D) shape?
questions.explain: A sphere is a solid 3D shape because it takes up space and is not flat.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A drawing of a circle on paper — is it a 2D shape or a 3D shape?
questions.explain: A circle drawn on paper is flat, so it is a 2D shape.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: When we read a book in English, which direction do our eyes move across a line?
questions.explain: In English we read from left to right across each line.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: When you finish reading one line in a book, where do your eyes go next?
options: To the right on the same line
To the line below on the left
To the top of the page
questions.explain: After finishing a line, we move down to the beginning of the next line.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Clap for each part of the word RAIN-BOW. How many claps do you make?
questions.explain: Rain-bow has two syllables, so you clap 2 times.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: The word BUTTERFLY has parts called syllables. How many syllables does BUT-TER-FLY have?
questions.explain: But-ter-fly has three syllables.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Which word rhymes with CAT?
questions.explain: Cat and hat both end with the -at sound, so they rhyme.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Which word rhymes with MOON?
questions.explain: Moon and spoon both end with the -oon sound, so they rhyme.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Do the words CAKE and LAKE rhyme?
options: No, they start with different letters
Yes, they both start with the same letter
questions.explain: Cake and lake both end with the -ake sound, so they do rhyme.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Listen to these word parts: /p/ ... /ig/. Blend them together. What word do you get?
questions.explain: Blending /p/ and /ig/ together makes the word pig.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: How many syllables does the word HAPPY have?
questions.explain: Hap-py has two syllables.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: What is the FIRST sound in the word SUN?
questions.explain: The first sound in sun is /s/, the letter S.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: What is the LAST sound in the word MOP?
questions.explain: The last sound in mop is /p/.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: What is the FIRST sound in the word FISH?
questions.explain: The first sound in fish is /f/.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Which letter makes the /b/ sound as in BALL?
questions.explain: The letter B makes the /b/ sound at the beginning of ball.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: What sound does the letter M make at the start of MILK?
questions.explain: The letter M makes the /m/ sound, as in milk.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Which letter makes the /t/ sound as in TOP?
questions.explain: The letter T makes the /t/ sound at the beginning of top.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: The word CAP has the letter A in the middle. Does the A in CAP make a SHORT or LONG vowel sound?
questions.explain: Cap has a short A sound, like the A in apple.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: The word KITE has the letter I. Does the I in KITE make a long or short sound?
questions.explain: Kite has a long I sound, like the I in ice cream.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Mia found a little puppy in the rain. She brought it inside and dried it with a towel. What did Mia use to dry the puppy?
questions.explain: The story says Mia dried the puppy with a towel.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Jake planted a seed in a pot. He watered it every day. One morning he saw a tiny green sprout! What did Jake see in the morning?
questions.explain: The story says Jake saw a tiny green sprout in the morning.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: In the story of The Tortoise and the Hare, the tortoise wins the race by going slowly but never stopping. What is the lesson of this story?
options: Slow and steady can win the race
You should take naps during a race
questions.explain: The lesson is that being slow but steady and never giving up can help you win.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: The first pig built a house of straw, the second pig built one of sticks, and the third pig built one of bricks. Which house was the strongest?
questions.explain: The brick house was the strongest and kept the wolf out.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: In the story of Goldilocks, a little girl visits a house in the forest. Who lives in that house?
questions.explain: Goldilocks visits the home of the Three Bears.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Lily and her dog Max ran to the park. They played near the big pond. What is the SETTING of this story?
questions.explain: The setting is the park near the big pond, where the story takes place.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Penguins are birds that cannot fly. They use their wings to swim very fast in cold ocean water. What do penguins use their wings for?
questions.explain: The text says penguins use their wings to swim fast in the ocean.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Bees live together in a hive. They make honey from flower nectar. Worker bees collect the nectar and bring it back home. Where do bees live?
options: In a nest in a tree
questions.explain: The text tells us that bees live together in a hive.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Which word is a NOUN (a person, place, or thing)?
questions.explain: Dog is a noun because it names a thing.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Which word is a VERB (an action word)?
questions.explain: Swim is a verb because it describes an action you can do.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Which word is an ADJECTIVE (a describing word)?
questions.explain: Fluffy is an adjective because it describes what something feels or looks like.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Plants need sunlight to grow. What else do plants need to stay alive?
questions.explain: Plants need water and soil along with sunlight to grow and stay alive.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which of these does NOT help a plant survive?
questions.explain: Plants need light, not darkness — darkness does not help them survive.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A dog drinks from its water bowl every day. Why do animals need water?
options: To keep their bodies working and stay alive
questions.explain: Animals need water to keep their bodies working properly and stay alive.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Maria forgot to water her plant for two weeks. The leaves turned yellow and drooped. What did the plant need?
questions.explain: The plant needed water — without it, leaves droop and turn yellow.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: You kick a soccer ball and it rolls forward. What kind of force did you use?
questions.explain: Kicking is a push force that makes the ball move forward.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A ball is rolling fast. You push it in the opposite direction. What happens to the ball?
options: It rolls faster in the same direction
questions.explain: Pushing a moving ball in the opposite direction makes it change direction.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: You pull a toy wagon toward you. The wagon starts moving. What made the wagon move?
questions.explain: Pulling the wagon with your hands caused it to move toward you.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: When you push a door open, the door pushes back on your hand a little. What does this show?
options: Objects in contact can push each other
questions.explain: When two objects touch, they can push or pull each other.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Two magnets are touching and one pushes the other away. What kind of force is this?
questions.explain: When magnets repel each other, they are pushing each other away.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: You touch the sidewalk on a sunny afternoon and it feels warm. What warmed the sidewalk?
questions.explain: Sunlight from the sun warms the sidewalk and other surfaces on Earth.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A dark rock sitting in the sun feels very hot. Where does this heat energy come from?
questions.explain: The sun's energy warms surfaces on Earth, and dark surfaces heat up more than light ones.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What tool do scientists use to measure how warm or cold it is outside?
questions.explain: A thermometer measures how warm or cold (the temperature) the air is.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: In winter it is often cold and snowy, and in summer it is often hot and sunny. What do we call the way weather repeats through the year?
questions.explain: When weather changes in a regular way over seasons, we call it a weather pattern.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Scientists noticed that it rains a lot in spring every year. This is an example of what?
questions.explain: When weather repeats in the same way each season, it is a weather pattern.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: On a map, the blue areas show water. What do the green or brown areas usually show?
questions.explain: On most maps, blue means water and green or brown areas show land.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A map of your school shows buildings, the playground, and a pond. What does the map help you do?
questions.explain: Maps help us find where things are located on Earth's surface.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: People build houses to protect themselves from rain, cold, and heat. What need does a house meet?
questions.explain: A house provides shelter, which protects people from weather and keeps them safe.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Farmers grow fruits and vegetables to feed people. How are farmers using their environment to meet people's needs?
options: They are using land to grow food
questions.explain: Farmers use land from the environment to grow food that people need to survive.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Your umbrella broke and you want to fix it so you stay dry in rain. What is the FIRST step an engineer would take?
options: Build a new umbrella right away
Ask questions and think about what the problem is
questions.explain: Engineers first ask questions and identify the problem before they start building a solution.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A class wants to build a paper bridge to hold a toy car. They try one design and it breaks. What should they do next?
options: Try a new design and test it again
Ask someone else to do it
questions.explain: In engineering, when a design does not work, you try a new idea and test it again.

questions.subject: social_studies
questions.prompt: This community helper drives a big red truck and uses a hose to put out fires. Who is this?
questions.explain: Firefighters ride red fire trucks and use hoses to put out fires and keep people safe.

questions.subject: social_studies
questions.prompt: A doctor works at a hospital and helps people when they are sick or hurt. What does a doctor do?
questions.explain: Doctors help sick or hurt people feel better and stay healthy.

questions.subject: social_studies
questions.prompt: This community helper wears a uniform and badge and helps keep people safe by following and enforcing community rules. Who is this?
questions.explain: Police officers wear uniforms and badges and help keep everyone safe in the community.

questions.subject: social_studies
questions.prompt: At school, we follow rules so that everyone stays safe and learns. Which is a good school rule?
options: Hit others when you are angry
questions.explain: Raising your hand before speaking is a good rule that helps everyone in class get a turn.

questions.subject: social_studies
questions.prompt: Who works in the school office and is the leader of the whole school?
questions.explain: The principal is the leader of the school and works in the school office.

questions.subject: social_studies
questions.prompt: A map is a drawing that shows us where places are. What does a map of your neighborhood show?
options: Where streets, parks, and buildings are located
How many people live in each house
questions.explain: A map shows where streets, buildings, parks, and other places are located.

questions.subject: social_studies
questions.prompt: A compass rose on a map shows four main directions. What are those four directions?
questions.explain: The four main compass directions are North, South, East, and West.

questions.subject: social_studies
questions.prompt: On a simple map of your classroom, a rectangle symbol shows the reading corner. What does the rectangle represent?
questions.explain: On a map, shapes like rectangles are symbols that represent real places or objects.

questions.subject: social_studies
questions.prompt: The American flag has stars and stripes. How many stripes does the American flag have?
questions.explain: The American flag has 13 stripes, one for each of the original 13 colonies.

questions.subject: social_studies
questions.prompt: The Statue of Liberty stands in New York Harbor. She holds a torch and a book. What does she represent?
options: Freedom and welcome for people coming to America
The president of the United States
questions.explain: The Statue of Liberty is a symbol of freedom and welcomes people who come to America.

questions.subject: social_studies
questions.prompt: The bald eagle is the national bird of the United States. Where does the bald eagle appear as a symbol?
options: On coins and the presidential seal
questions.explain: The bald eagle appears on coins, the presidential seal, and other official U.S. symbols.

questions.subject: social_studies
questions.prompt: There are four seasons in a year. Which season comes after winter?
questions.explain: Spring comes after winter — it gets warmer and flowers begin to bloom.

questions.subject: social_studies
questions.prompt: How many days are in a week?
questions.explain: There are 7 days in one week: Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, and Saturday.

questions.subject: social_studies
questions.prompt: December, January, and February are usually cold months in New York. What season do these months belong to?
questions.explain: December, January, and February are the winter months when it is coldest.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: There are 7 pigeons on a park bench in Central Park. 5 more pigeons land on the bench. How many pigeons are on the bench now?
questions.explain: 7 + 5 = 12 pigeons on the bench.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Rosa saw 14 students on the subway. 6 students got off at the next stop. How many students are still on the subway?
questions.explain: 14 minus 6 = 8 students remain on the subway.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: There were 15 kids playing in Prospect Park. Some kids went home. Now there are 9 kids left. How many kids went home?
questions.explain: 15 minus 9 = 6 kids went home.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Marcus had some stickers. He gave 8 to his friend at school. Now he has 7 stickers left. How many stickers did Marcus start with?
questions.explain: Marcus started with 7 + 8 = 15 stickers.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 4 + 5 + 6?

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Sam has 3 red crayons, 7 blue crayons, and 3 green crayons. How many crayons does Sam have in all?
questions.explain: 3 + 7 + 3 = 13 crayons in all.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which equation shows that you can add numbers in any order and get the same sum?
questions.explain: 3 + 5 = 5 + 3 shows the commutative property; order does not change the sum.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which is the easiest way to add (2 + 8) + 4?
options: Add 2 and 4 first to get 6, then add 8
Add 8 and 4 first to get 12, then add 2
Add 2 and 8 first to make 10, then add 4
questions.explain: Adding 2 + 8 = 10 first uses the associative property to make a friendly ten, then 10 + 4 = 14.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What number makes this true? ___ + 6 = 13

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Mia needs to solve 15 minus 8. Which addition fact helps her?
questions.explain: 7 + 8 = 15 means 15 minus 8 = 7.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Leo counts on from 8 to find 8 + 3. What numbers does he say?
questions.explain: Counting on 3 from 8 gives 9, 10, 11, so 8 + 3 = 11.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: There are 12 apples. You count back 4 to subtract. What number do you land on?
questions.explain: Counting back 4 from 12: 11, 10, 9, 8 -- you land on 8.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 9 + 7?

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 13 minus 5?
questions.explain: 13 minus 5 = 8 (think: 5 + 8 = 13).

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Anaya uses the doubles strategy to solve 6 + 7. Which shows the doubles-plus-one approach?
options: Count up from 1 all the way to 13
Take away 1 from 7 to get 6, then double 6
questions.explain: 6 + 6 = 12, and 6 + 7 is one more than 6 + 6, so 6 + 7 = 13.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which equation is TRUE?
questions.explain: 7 + 3 = 10 is the only equation where both sides have the same value.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What does the equal sign mean in 4 + 6 = 10?
options: The answer always comes after it
Both sides have the same value
questions.explain: The equal sign means both sides of the equation have the same value.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is the missing number? 9 + ___ = 14

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is the missing number? 17 minus ___ = 9
questions.explain: 17 minus 8 = 9, so the missing number is 8.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What number comes right after 109 when counting?
questions.explain: When counting by ones, 110 comes right after 109.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: How do you write one hundred fifteen as a numeral?
questions.explain: One hundred fifteen is written as 115.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: The number 34 has ___ tens and ___ ones.
questions.explain: 34 = 3 tens (30) and 4 ones.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which number has 6 tens and 2 ones?
questions.explain: 6 tens = 60 and 2 ones = 2, so the number is 62.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Ben has 5 groups of ten blocks and 8 single blocks. What number do his blocks show?
questions.explain: 5 groups of ten = 50, plus 8 ones = 58.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which symbol goes in the box? 47 ___ 74
questions.explain: 47 is less than 74, so we use the < symbol.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which statement about 63 and 36 is TRUE?
questions.explain: 63 > 36 because 63 has more tens (6 tens vs. 3 tens).

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 36 + 20?
questions.explain: 36 + 20 = 56 (add 2 tens: 3 + 2 = 5 tens, ones stay as 6).

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 45 + 37?

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 10 more than 53?
questions.explain: 10 more than 53 is 63 -- the tens digit goes up by 1.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 10 less than 80?
questions.explain: 10 less than 80 is 70 -- the tens digit goes down by 1.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 70 minus 30?
questions.explain: 70 minus 30 = 40 (subtract the tens: 7 minus 3 = 4 tens = 40).

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 90 minus 60?
questions.explain: 90 minus 60 = 30 (subtract the tens: 9 minus 6 = 3 tens = 30).

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Three pencils are 4 inches, 7 inches, and 5 inches long. Which order goes from shortest to longest?
questions.explain: Shortest to longest: 4 inches, 5 inches, 7 inches.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Keisha has a ribbon, a crayon, and a book. The ribbon is longer than the crayon. The book is shorter than the crayon. Which object is the longest?
questions.explain: The ribbon is longer than the crayon, and the crayon is longer than the book, so the ribbon is longest.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A shelf is measured using paper clips placed end to end. It takes 9 paper clips to span the shelf. How long is the shelf?
questions.explain: The length is expressed as 9 paper clips -- we name the unit we used to measure.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A book is 6 large paper clips long. If you measure it with small paper clips, will you need more or fewer small clips?
options: You cannot measure with small clips
questions.explain: Smaller units are shorter, so you need more of them to cover the same length.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: The clock has the hour hand on 3 and the minute hand on 12. What time is it?
questions.explain: When the minute hand points to 12, read the hour hand -- it shows 3:00.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: The minute hand points to 6 and the hour hand points between 7 and 8. What time does the clock show?
questions.explain: When the minute hand is on 6, it shows 30 minutes past the hour, so the time is 7:30.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: School ends at half past 2 in the afternoon. How do you write that time?
questions.explain: Half past 2 means 30 minutes after 2 o'clock, written as 2:30.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A class voted for their favorite park: 5 picked Central Park, 3 picked Riverside Park, 7 picked Prospect Park. How many students voted in all?
questions.explain: 5 + 3 + 7 = 15 students voted in all.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A tally chart shows: Dogs -- 6, Cats -- 4, Fish -- 2. How many more students chose dogs than fish?
questions.explain: 6 minus 2 = 4 more students chose dogs than fish.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which shape has exactly 4 equal sides and 4 corners?
questions.explain: A square has exactly 4 equal sides and 4 corners.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which shape has NO corners and NO straight sides?
questions.explain: A circle has no corners and no straight sides -- it is perfectly round.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which two flat shapes can you put together to make a larger rectangle?
questions.explain: Two right triangles placed together along their longest sides form a rectangle.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A pizza is cut into 2 equal parts. Each part is called a ___.
questions.explain: When a whole is divided into 2 equal parts, each part is one half.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A rectangle is divided into 4 equal parts. What is each part called?
questions.explain: When a whole is divided into 4 equal parts, each part is one quarter (one fourth).

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Which word has the long 'a' sound spelled with the a_e pattern (like in 'name')?
questions.explain: The word 'cake' follows the a_e pattern (a-consonant-e) that makes a long 'a' sound.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Which word has the long 'e' sound?
questions.explain: The word 'feet' uses the ee spelling to make the long 'e' sound.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Which word has the long 'o' sound spelled with the oa pattern?
questions.explain: The word 'boat' uses the oa spelling to make the long 'o' sound.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Sound out each letter. What word do these sounds make? /s/ /u/ /n/
questions.explain: Blending /s/ /u/ /n/ gives the word 'sun.'

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Which word uses a short vowel sound and rhymes with 'hop'?
questions.explain: The word 'top' has a short 'o' sound and rhymes with 'hop.'

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: How many syllables does the word 'rabbit' have?
questions.explain: The word 'rabbit' has 2 syllables: rab-bit.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Which word has TWO syllables?
questions.explain: The word 'garden' has 2 syllables: gar-den.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: A good reader reads smoothly. When you see a period at the end of a sentence, what should you do?
options: Pause briefly before the next sentence
questions.explain: A period signals a brief pause before moving on to the next sentence.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: When reading aloud, which example shows the best fluent reading?
options: The... cat... sat... on... a... mat.
The cat sat on a mat.
THE CAT SAT ON A MAT!
questions.explain: Fluent reading means saying words smoothly and naturally, like normal speech.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Which group shows all four letters correctly written as uppercase (capital) letters?
questions.explain: A, B, C, D are all correctly printed uppercase letters.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Which word is a PROPER noun?
questions.explain: Central Park is a proper noun because it is the specific name of a place and starts with capital letters.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a POSSESSIVE noun correctly?
options: The bone of dog is big.
questions.explain: "The dog's bone" correctly uses an apostrophe and s to show the bone belongs to the dog.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Which sentence is written in the PAST tense?
questions.explain: 'Jumped' is the past tense form of 'jump,' showing the action already happened.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Read this sentence: 'The puppy was so tiny that it fit in my pocket.' What does the word TINY mean?
questions.explain: The clue 'fit in my pocket' tells us that tiny means very small.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Read this sentence: 'After running all the way home, Jada was exhausted and could barely keep her eyes open.' What does EXHAUSTED mean?
questions.explain: The clue 'could barely keep her eyes open' after running tells us exhausted means very tired.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this: 'The frog jumped into the pond. It splashed in the cool water. The frog swam to a lily pad and sat very still.' Where did the frog swim to?
questions.explain: The story says the frog swam to a lily pad and sat very still.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this: 'Max woke up early. He put on his boots and raincoat. Then he ran outside to jump in puddles.' Why did Max put on his boots and raincoat?
options: He was cold inside the house
He wanted to jump in puddles outside
He was going swimming at the pool
questions.explain: Max put on his boots and raincoat so he could go outside and jump in puddles.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this: 'Lily found a small blue egg in the garden. She put it in a nest of soft leaves. One morning, a tiny bird hatched and chirped loudly.' What happened after Lily put the egg in the nest?
options: A tiny bird hatched from the egg
questions.explain: After Lily put the egg in the nest of soft leaves, a tiny bird hatched and chirped loudly.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this: 'A bear was very hungry. He looked for berries in the forest. He found a big bush and ate until he was full. Then he went back to his cave to sleep.' What is the best retelling?
options: A bear went to sleep in a cave.
A bear was hungry, found and ate berries, then went to sleep.
There were lots of berries in the forest.
A bear liked to walk in the forest every day.
questions.explain: A good retelling covers the beginning, middle, and end: the bear was hungry, found berries, ate them, then slept.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this: 'Zoe always left crumbs on the table. One day, a parade of ants found the crumbs. Zoe learned to clean up, and the ants never came back.' What is the message of this story?
options: Cleaning up helps keep pests away.
Zoe does not like being in the kitchen.
questions.explain: The story's message is that keeping things clean -- like wiping up crumbs -- helps keep pests away.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this: 'Sofia lived in a small house near the river. She loved to fish every morning before school. One day, she caught the biggest fish she had ever seen!' Where does this story take place?
questions.explain: The story says Sofia lived near the river -- the river is the setting.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this: 'Benny the dog was lonely all day. His family was away at work and school. When they came home, Benny wagged his tail and jumped with joy.' How does Benny feel when his family comes home?
questions.explain: Benny wags his tail and jumps with joy, which shows he is happy to see his family.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this: 'I went to the store with my mom. I picked out apples and bananas. Then we walked home together.' Who is telling this story?
questions.explain: The word 'I' shows that the child who experienced the event is the narrator.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this: 'Maria skipped to the park. She found a shiny penny on the bench. She put it in her pocket and smiled all day.' Who is telling this story?
options: Maria is telling it using I
An outside narrator tells it using she
Maria's friend is telling it using you
questions.explain: The story uses 'she' and 'her' instead of 'I,' so an outside narrator is telling the story.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this: 'The girl in the picture is wearing a big yellow hat. She is standing in a garden with flowers all around her.' What does the illustration help you understand?
options: What the girl looks like and where she is
questions.explain: Illustrations help readers picture what characters look like and where they are.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this: 'The dragon spread its wide, green wings. The picture shows a huge dragon soaring over a tall mountain.' How does the picture add to the story?
options: It tells us the dragon's name
It shows what the dragon and the setting look like
It explains why the dragon is flying
It reveals the ending of the story
questions.explain: Illustrations add detail about what characters and settings look like, helping readers visualize the story.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this: 'Penguins are birds that cannot fly. They use their wings as flippers to swim very fast. Penguins live in cold places like Antarctica.' What do penguins use their wings for?
options: To fly high in the sky
To keep warm in cold weather
To swim fast in the water
To build nests for their eggs
questions.explain: The text says penguins use their wings as flippers to swim very fast.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this: 'Bees collect nectar from flowers. They bring it back to the hive. There, bees turn the nectar into honey.' According to the text, where do bees bring the nectar?
questions.explain: The text says bees bring nectar back to the hive, where it becomes honey.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this: 'Butterflies start as eggs. Then they become caterpillars. Next they form a chrysalis. Finally, they become beautiful butterflies.' What is the main topic?
options: The life cycle of a butterfly
questions.explain: The passage describes all the stages of a butterfly's life, so the life cycle is the main topic.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this: 'Rain falls from clouds. It fills rivers and lakes. Plants drink water through their roots. Animals drink from rivers and lakes.' What is the best title?
questions.explain: The passage shows how rain provides water for both plants and animals, making 'How Rain Helps Living Things' the best title.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this: 'In spring, flowers start to bloom. The warm weather helps seeds grow. Bees come out to drink nectar from the flowers.' What causes the seeds to grow?
questions.explain: The text says the warm weather helps the seeds grow -- warm weather is the cause.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this: 'When it rains a lot, rivers can overflow. Overflowing rivers can flood nearby towns. Floods can damage roads and homes.' What is the connection between heavy rain and flooding?
options: Rain makes rivers smaller over time
Heavy rain causes rivers to overflow, which leads to floods
Floods make it rain even more
Heavy rain only damages homes directly
questions.explain: Heavy rain causes rivers to overflow, and overflowing rivers cause floods -- this is a cause-and-effect chain.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What do roots do for a plant?
options: Absorb water and nutrients from the soil
questions.explain: Roots anchor the plant and absorb water and nutrients from the soil.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A dog has thick fur in winter. How does this external structure help the dog survive?
options: Helps the dog run faster through snow
Keeps the dog warm in cold weather
Helps the dog find food under snow
Helps the dog swim better in cold water
questions.explain: Thick fur is an external structure that insulates the dog and keeps it warm in cold weather.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A cactus stores water in its thick stem. How does this structure help the cactus survive?
options: It helps the cactus grow much taller than other plants
It helps the cactus make more seeds quickly
It helps the cactus survive in dry places with little rain
It helps the cactus attract more animals to pollinate it
questions.explain: Storing water in a thick stem lets the cactus survive in dry desert environments with little rainfall.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A mother hen sits on her eggs to keep them warm. How does this behavior help her offspring?
options: It teaches the chicks to fly later on
It keeps the eggs warm so the chicks can hatch
It finds worms for the chicks to eat
It protects the eggs from falling rain
questions.explain: Sitting on eggs keeps them at the right temperature so the chicks can develop and hatch.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A mother wolf teaches her pups to hunt. How does this behavior help the wolf pups survive?
options: It helps them build safe dens in snow
It helps them survive by learning to find their own food
It helps them grow thicker fur in winter
It keeps them away from other packs of wolves
questions.explain: Teaching pups to hunt is a parent behavior that helps offspring survive by learning to get their own food.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A kitten has the same fur color as its mother. This feature passed from parent to offspring is called a(n) ___.
questions.explain: Traits passed from parents to offspring, like fur color, are called inherited traits.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Two brown dogs have puppies. Some puppies are brown and some are black. What does this tell us about inherited traits?
options: All offspring always look exactly the same as both parents
Offspring inherit traits but can vary from their parents
Black fur is not an inherited trait in dogs
The puppies got their color from the environment
questions.explain: Offspring inherit traits from parents but can vary -- not every offspring looks exactly like its parents.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of a trait that an offspring INHERITS from its parents?
options: A dog learning to sit on command from its owner
A tree growing taller each year from sunlight
A puppy born with floppy ears just like its parent
A bird flying south for winter when temperatures drop
questions.explain: A puppy born with floppy ears like its parent is an inherited trait -- it was passed down genetically, not learned.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: You pluck a guitar string and hear a sound. What is making the sound?
options: Air blowing through the guitar body
The string vibrating back and forth
Your fingers warming up the string
The wood of the guitar expanding
questions.explain: Sound is made when an object vibrates -- the plucked string vibrates to produce sound.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A drum makes sound when you hit it. If you press your hand on the drum right after hitting it, what happens?
options: The sound stops because the vibrations stop
The sound changes to a higher pitch
Nothing happens to the sound at all
questions.explain: Pressing your hand on the drum stops the vibrations, which stops the sound.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: You shine a flashlight across a dark room. How does the light travel from the flashlight?
questions.explain: Light always travels in straight lines outward from its source.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: When light hits a mirror and bounces back, what is this bouncing called?
questions.explain: When light bounces off a smooth surface like a mirror, it is called reflection.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A beam of light enters a glass of water and bends. What happens when light passes from air into water?
options: Light stops completely at the surface
Light travels much faster inside water
Light bends as it moves from one material into another
Light reflects straight back the same way it came in
questions.explain: When light moves from one material (air) into another (water), it bends -- this is called refraction.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: You are in a completely dark room. Can you see the toys on the floor?
options: Yes, because your eyes adjust after a few minutes
No, because there is no light to illuminate the toys
Yes, if the toys are bright colors
Yes, because some light always leaks under the door
questions.explain: Objects can only be seen when light shines on them -- without any light, nothing can be seen.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A shadow forms behind a tree when the sun shines on it. What causes the shadow?
options: The tree absorbs all nearby heat from the sun
The tree blocks the straight-traveling light, leaving a dark area
Darkness falls down from the tree like rain
The tree reflects all light backward toward the sun
questions.explain: Because light travels in straight lines, the tree blocks the light and creates a shadow behind it.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: The sun rises in the morning and sets in the evening every single day. What kind of pattern is this?
questions.explain: The sun rising and setting every day is a daily pattern we can observe in the sky.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Why can we see stars at night but not during the day?
options: Stars only come out at night and hide during the day
The sun is so bright during the day that it makes stars impossible to see
Stars move to the other side of Earth during daylight
Clouds always block stars during the daytime
questions.explain: Stars are always in the sky, but sunlight is so bright during the day that it drowns out the faint light of stars.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: In summer, days are longer. In winter, days are shorter. What changes between summer and winter?
options: The distance between Earth and the moon
The number of hours of daylight each day
How brightly stars shine at night
How fast the sun moves across the sky
questions.explain: The number of hours of daylight changes with the seasons -- summer has more daylight hours and winter has fewer.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which season has the MOST hours of daylight?
questions.explain: Summer has the most hours of daylight because the sun rises earliest and sets latest.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: In which season does the sun set the EARLIEST in the evening?
questions.explain: In winter, the sun sets earliest in the evening because winter has the fewest hours of daylight.

questions.subject: social_studies
questions.prompt: Which is an example of a family TRADITION?
options: Having a special dinner together every year on a holiday
Watching TV in the evening sometimes
Doing homework after school each day
questions.explain: A tradition is something families do regularly in a special way, like a yearly holiday dinner.

questions.subject: social_studies
questions.prompt: Which statement about families is TRUE?
options: All families must have exactly two parents
All families must live in the same house always
Families can be different sizes and have different members
All families speak the same language at home
questions.explain: Families come in all shapes and sizes -- some have one parent, some include grandparents, and they may speak different languages.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Maria counted 34 books on the library shelf. Then 18 more books were returned. How many books are on the shelf now?
questions.explain: 34 + 18 = 52 books on the shelf.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A pizza shop sold 56 slices in the morning and 27 slices in the afternoon. How many slices were sold in all?
questions.explain: 56 + 27 = 83 slices were sold in total.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: There were 75 pigeons in Central Park. Then 38 flew away. Later, 12 more landed. How many pigeons are in the park now?
questions.explain: 75 minus 38 equals 37, then 37 plus 12 equals 49 pigeons in the park.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: The subway train had 63 riders. At the first stop, 29 riders got off and 14 got on. How many riders are on the train now?
questions.explain: 63 minus 29 equals 34, then 34 plus 14 equals 48 riders on the train.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 9 + 7?

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 18 minus 9?
questions.explain: 18 minus 9 = 9.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 7 + 8?

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Is the number 14 odd or even?
questions.explain: 14 is even because it can be split into two equal groups of 7.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which number is ODD?
questions.explain: 17 is odd because it cannot be split into two equal whole-number groups.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: An egg carton has 3 rows with 4 eggs in each row. How many eggs are there in all?
questions.explain: 3 rows times 4 eggs equals 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 eggs.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A window has 5 rows of squares with 3 squares in each row. How many squares are there?
questions.explain: 5 rows times 3 squares equals 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 15 squares.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: In the number 347, what does the digit 3 represent?
questions.explain: In 347, the digit 3 is in the hundreds place, so it represents 3 hundreds or 300.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is the value of the digit 5 in the number 256?
questions.explain: In 256, the digit 5 is in the tens place, so its value is 50.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which number has 4 hundreds, 0 tens, and 8 ones?
questions.explain: 4 hundreds + 0 tens + 8 ones = 400 + 0 + 8 = 408.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Count by 5s. What number comes next? 25, 30, 35, ___
questions.explain: When counting by 5s, 35 + 5 = 40.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Count by 10s. What number comes next? 460, 470, 480, ___
questions.explain: When counting by 10s, 480 + 10 = 490.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Count by 100s. What number comes next? 200, 300, 400, ___
questions.explain: When counting by 100s, 400 + 100 = 500.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: How do you write five hundred twelve in numbers?
questions.explain: Five hundred twelve = 500 + 12 = 512.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is another way to write 730?
questions.explain: 730 is written as seven hundred thirty because 7 is in the hundreds place and 3 is in the tens place.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which symbol makes this true? 456 ___ 465
questions.explain: 456 < 465 because both have 4 hundreds, but 456 has 5 tens while 465 has 6 tens.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which number is GREATER than 389?
questions.explain: 391 > 389 because both have 3 hundreds and 8 tens, but 391 has 1 one more than 389's 9 ones — wait, 391 has 9 tens and 389 has 8 tens, so 391 is greater.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 64 + 27?

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 82 minus 35?
questions.explain: 82 minus 35 = 47; you can check by adding 35 + 47 = 82.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 93 minus 48?
questions.explain: 93 minus 48 = 45; think 93 minus 40 = 53, then 53 minus 8 = 45.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 425 + 163?

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 600 minus 247?

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 10 more than 342?
questions.explain: 10 more than 342 is 342 + 10 = 352; only the tens digit changes.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is 100 less than 750?
questions.explain: 100 less than 750 is 750 minus 100 = 650; only the hundreds digit changes.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which tool would you use to measure the length of a book?
questions.explain: A ruler is used to measure the length of objects like books.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A pencil is 7 inches long. A crayon is 4 inches long. How much longer is the pencil than the crayon?
questions.explain: 7 minus 4 = 3 inches; the pencil is 3 inches longer than the crayon.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A red ribbon is 12 cm long. A blue ribbon is 7 cm long. How much longer is the red ribbon?
questions.explain: 12 minus 7 = 5 cm; the red ribbon is 5 centimeters longer.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Lily's jump rope is 48 inches long. She needs it to be 60 inches. How many more inches does she need?
questions.explain: 60 minus 48 = 12 inches more are needed.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: One hallway in a NYC school is 35 feet long. Another hallway is 27 feet long. What is the total length of both hallways?
questions.explain: 35 + 27 = 62 feet total.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A clock shows the hour hand pointing between 3 and 4, and the minute hand pointing at 9. What time does the clock show?
questions.explain: When the minute hand points to 9, it shows 45 minutes, so the time is 3:45.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: School starts at 8:30 AM. The clock now shows 8:05 AM. How many minutes until school starts?
questions.explain: From 8:05 to 8:30 is 25 minutes.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: You have 2 quarters, 1 dime, and 3 pennies. How much money is that?
questions.explain: 2 quarters = 50 cents, 1 dime = 10 cents, 3 pennies = 3 cents; 50 + 10 + 3 = 63 cents.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A juice box costs 75 cents. You pay with 1 dollar. How much change do you get?
questions.explain: 100 cents minus 75 cents = 25 cents change.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: You want to buy a snack for 85 cents. You have 3 quarters and 1 dime. Do you have enough money?
options: Yes, you have 85 cents — wait, 3 quarters = 75 cents + 1 dime = 85 cents. Yes, exactly enough!
questions.explain: 3 quarters = 75 cents plus 1 dime = 10 cents equals 85 cents, which is exactly enough.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Students measured their pencils. The lengths in inches were: 4, 5, 4, 6, 5, 5, 4. How many pencils were 5 inches long?
questions.explain: Counting the 5s in the list: there are 3 pencils that are 5 inches long.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A bar graph shows: apples = 8, bananas = 5, oranges = 6. How many more apples than bananas are there?
questions.explain: 8 minus 5 = 3 more apples than bananas.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A picture graph shows students' favorite pets: cats = 4, dogs = 7, fish = 3. How many students were surveyed in all?
questions.explain: 4 + 7 + 3 = 14 students were surveyed.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which shape has exactly 4 equal sides and 4 equal corners?
questions.explain: A square has exactly 4 sides that are all the same length and 4 equal right-angle corners.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which shape has 5 sides?
questions.explain: A pentagon has exactly 5 sides.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A rectangle is divided into 3 rows and 4 columns of equal squares. How many small squares are there in total?
questions.explain: 3 rows times 4 columns = 12 equal squares.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A pizza is cut into 4 equal pieces. Your friend eats 1 piece. What fraction of the pizza did your friend eat?
questions.explain: 1 piece out of 4 equal pieces is 1/4 (one-fourth) of the pizza.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A circle is divided into 3 equal parts. If 2 parts are shaded, what fraction is shaded?
questions.explain: 2 out of 3 equal parts are shaded, which is 2/3 (two-thirds).

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Which word has a LONG vowel sound?
questions.explain: The word 'cake' has a long A sound because of the silent E at the end.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Which word has a SHORT vowel sound?
questions.explain: The word 'jump' has a short U sound.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Which pair of words both have the long A sound?
questions.explain: Both 'rain' and 'train' have the long A sound spelled with the 'ai' vowel pattern.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: What does the prefix 're-' mean in the word 'redo'?
questions.explain: The prefix 're-' means again, so 'redo' means to do again.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: What does the suffix '-ful' mean in the word 'helpful'?
questions.explain: The suffix '-ful' means full of, so 'helpful' means full of help.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: When reading aloud, what should you do when you see a period at the end of a sentence?
questions.explain: A period signals the end of a sentence, so a reader pauses briefly before continuing.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Which describes a FLUENT reader best?
options: Sounds out each letter one at a time
questions.explain: A fluent reader reads smoothly at a good pace and uses expression to show meaning.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this passage: 'Mia and her dog Rex went to the park. Rex chased a squirrel up a tree. Mia laughed and called Rex back. They sat under a big oak tree to rest.' WHO went to the park?
questions.explain: The passage says 'Mia and her dog Rex went to the park.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this passage: 'Every morning, Leo made his bed and fed his goldfish Bubbles. He loved taking care of Bubbles. One day, Leo noticed that Bubbles was not eating. Leo told his mom, and they took Bubbles to the pet store for help.' WHY did Leo go to the pet store?
options: Because he forgot to feed Bubbles
questions.explain: The passage says Leo went to the pet store because Bubbles was not eating.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this passage: 'The old library on Oak Street had thousands of books. Sam visited every Saturday. He always picked two books: one about animals and one about space. The librarian, Mrs. Chen, saved the newest animal books just for him.' HOW did Mrs. Chen help Sam?
options: She drove him to the library
She saved the newest animal books for him
She helped him find space books
questions.explain: The passage states that Mrs. Chen saved the newest animal books just for Sam.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this passage: 'Zara was nervous about her first day at a new school. She sat alone at lunch until a girl named Priya said, Do you want to sit with us? Zara smiled and felt much better. By the end of the day, she had made three new friends.' How did Zara respond when Priya invited her to sit together?
options: She said no and kept sitting alone
She smiled and felt much better
She cried and called her mom
questions.explain: The passage says 'Zara smiled and felt much better' after Priya's kind invitation.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this passage: 'Jake loved to play soccer, but one week he broke his arm. He could not play. Jake sat on the bench sadly. His coach said, You can be our team helper and water carrier! Jake felt proud and important.' How did Jake change after what his coach said?
options: He learned to play with one arm
questions.explain: After his coach gave him a new role, Jake felt proud and important.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this passage: 'The little brook went giggle, giggle, giggle as it tumbled over the rocks. It danced through the meadow, singing to the flowers.' What does the word 'giggle' tell you about the brook?
options: The brook is dark and scary
The brook makes a playful, happy sound
The brook is very large and deep
questions.explain: The word 'giggle' is a playful, happy sound, which tells us the brook sounds cheerful.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this passage: 'The old house groaned and creaked in the storm. Every window rattled, and the door howled as the wind pushed it open.' The words groaned, creaked, and howled make the house seem —
questions.explain: Words like 'groaned,' 'creaked,' and 'howled' are eerie sounds that make the house seem scary and alive.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this passage: 'One morning, Lily found a tiny bird with a hurt wing. She made a cozy nest box for it and fed it every day. After two weeks, the bird was healed. Lily opened the window, and the bird flew away into the blue sky.' What is the ENDING of this story?
options: Lily fed the bird every day
questions.explain: The ending of the story is when the healed bird flew away into the sky.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: In most stories, what happens in the BEGINNING?
questions.explain: At the beginning of a story, the characters and setting are introduced so readers know who and where.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this passage: 'Ben thought the roller coaster looked amazing and zoomed to get in line. His little sister, Ava, stared up at the tall ride and whispered, I do not want to go on that.' How do Ben and Ava feel DIFFERENTLY about the roller coaster?
options: Ben is scared; Ava is excited
Ben is excited; Ava is scared
questions.explain: Ben thinks it looks amazing and rushes to the line, while Ava is afraid and does not want to ride.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this passage: 'Mom said the mess in the kitchen needed to be cleaned up right away. Carlos thought it was not that bad — just a few crumbs.' Whose point of view is that the kitchen is very messy?
questions.explain: Mom thinks the mess needs to be cleaned right away, showing she sees it as very messy.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this passage: 'Bees are very important insects. They collect nectar from flowers to make honey. As they move from flower to flower, they carry pollen, which helps plants grow new seeds. Without bees, many plants could not survive.' What do bees carry from flower to flower?
questions.explain: The passage states that bees carry pollen from flower to flower, which helps plants grow new seeds.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this passage: 'The Arctic is one of the coldest places on Earth. Polar bears have thick fur and a layer of fat to stay warm. Their white fur helps them hide in the snow while hunting. Polar bears are excellent swimmers and can swim for many miles.' Why is a polar bear's white fur important?
options: It helps them hide in the snow
questions.explain: The passage says their white fur helps them hide in the snow while hunting.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this passage: 'Volcanoes are openings in Earth's surface. When a volcano erupts, hot melted rock called lava flows out. Lava can destroy everything in its path. Over time, cooled lava creates new land. Some islands, like Hawaii, were formed by volcanoes.' What is lava?
options: Hot melted rock from a volcano
Steam and smoke from a mountain
questions.explain: The passage defines lava as hot melted rock that flows out when a volcano erupts.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this passage: 'Dogs make great pets. They are loyal and love to play. Dogs can be trained to follow commands like sit and stay. Some dogs even help people by guiding those who cannot see. Dogs come in many shapes and sizes.' What is the MAIN TOPIC of this passage?
questions.explain: The whole passage is about why dogs make great pets.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this passage: 'Recycling helps our planet. When we recycle paper, we save trees. Recycling cans and bottles uses less energy than making new ones. Communities that recycle create less trash. Everyone can help by putting the right things in the recycling bin.' What is the MAIN TOPIC?
questions.explain: The passage is mostly about how recycling helps our planet.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this passage: 'The desert is an arid place. Very little rain falls there, and the sun beats down all day. Only special plants and animals can survive in such a dry land.' The word ARID means —
questions.explain: The passage says arid places get very little rain and are dry, so arid means very dry.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this passage: 'Butterflies go through a remarkable transformation. They start as eggs, hatch into caterpillars, form a chrysalis, and finally emerge as beautiful butterflies. This amazing change is called metamorphosis.' The word TRANSFORMATION means —
questions.explain: The passage uses 'transformation' to describe the amazing complete change butterflies go through.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this passage: 'Always wash your hands before eating. Germs can spread from your hands to your food and make you sick. Use soap and warm water and scrub for at least 20 seconds.' Why did the author MOST LIKELY write this passage?
options: To entertain readers with a funny story
To teach readers how to stay healthy
To explain how soap is made
questions.explain: The author's purpose is to inform and teach readers how to stay healthy by washing their hands.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses an ADJECTIVE correctly?
questions.explain: 'Tall' is an adjective that describes the boy — adjectives describe nouns.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Which word is an ADVERB in this sentence: 'The rabbit hopped quickly across the yard.'?
questions.explain: 'Quickly' is an adverb because it describes HOW the rabbit hopped.

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Where does the comma go in a letter greeting like 'Dear Grandma'?
questions.explain: In the greeting of a letter, a comma goes after the name: 'Dear Grandma,'

questions.subject: literacy
questions.prompt: Read this sentence: 'The baby bird was so tiny that it fit in the palm of her hand.' What does TINY mean?
questions.explain: The clue 'it fit in the palm of her hand' tells us tiny means very small.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which property tells you how something FEELS when you touch it?
questions.explain: Texture describes how something feels when you touch it, such as rough, smooth, or bumpy.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A scientist describes an object as smooth, shiny, hard, and silver. Which object fits BEST?
questions.explain: A silver spoon is smooth, shiny, hard, and silver in color.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which of these materials is the most FLEXIBLE?
questions.explain: A rubber band is the most flexible because it can be stretched and bent without breaking.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: You want to find out which material is the HARDEST. What test should you do?
options: Try to scratch each material with a coin
Look at the color of each material
questions.explain: A scratch test is a good way to test hardness — harder materials are harder to scratch.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A student bends four materials. Paper bends easily, wood barely bends, plastic bends a little, and steel does not bend at all. Which material is the LEAST flexible?
questions.explain: Steel does not bend at all, making it the least flexible material in the test.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Why can't you see the tiny particles that make up a piece of sugar?
options: They are too small to see
questions.explain: Matter is made of particles too small to be seen with just our eyes.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: When salt disappears into water, where does it go?
options: Its tiny particles mix throughout the water
questions.explain: Salt is made of tiny particles that spread throughout the water even though we cannot see them.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What happens to butter when you heat it in a pan?
questions.explain: Heat causes butter to melt, changing it from a solid to a liquid.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Water is left in a freezer overnight. What will happen to the water?
options: The water will freeze into ice
questions.explain: When temperature drops below freezing, liquid water changes to solid ice.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: How do bees help flowers make seeds?
options: Bees carry pollen from flower to flower
questions.explain: Bees pollinate flowers by carrying pollen from one flower to another, which helps plants make seeds.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A bird eats a berry and flies far away. Later, a seed from the berry grows into a new plant. How did the bird help the plant?
options: The bird spread the seed to a new place
The bird gave the plant sunlight
questions.explain: Birds help disperse seeds by eating fruits and dropping seeds far from the parent plant.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which animal is MOST LIKELY to help pollinate flowers?
questions.explain: Butterflies visit flowers to drink nectar and carry pollen from flower to flower, helping pollination.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which animal would you MOST LIKELY find living in a rainforest?
questions.explain: Toucans live in rainforests where there are many tall trees and plenty of fruit to eat.

questions.subject: science
