questions.explain: Captions are the words written under or next to a photo. They tell you what the picture is showing or explain more about it.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: You would use a GLOSSARY to find ___.
questions.explain: A glossary is like a mini-dictionary at the back of a book. You use it to find the meaning of difficult or special words in the book.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Where would you look to find which PAGE a chapter starts on?
questions.explain: The table of contents is at the front of a book and lists all the chapters with their page numbers.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: A map in a book about animals would help you understand ___.
options: what the animals look like up close
where the animals live in the world
questions.explain: Maps show places and locations. A map in an animal book would show you WHERE in the world those animals live.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: A story uses 'I' and 'me' throughout. It is told from ___ point of view.
questions.explain: When the narrator uses 'I' and 'me,' the story is in FIRST PERSON. The narrator is telling the story as if it happened to them.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: The story says: 'She ran home as fast as she could.' What point of view is this?
questions.explain: When the story uses 'she,' 'he,' or 'they' to talk about characters, it is THIRD PERSON point of view. The narrator is not in the story.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence is written in FIRST PERSON point of view?
questions.explain: 'I cannot wait for summer!' uses the word 'I,' which is a first-person clue word. The narrator is speaking about themselves.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: What clue word tells you a story is in FIRST PERSON?
questions.explain: The word 'I' is the key clue for first person. When the narrator says 'I did this' or 'I felt that,' the story is in first person.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this: 'I love going to the beach. My favorite part is looking for shells.' Who is telling this story?
questions.explain: The words 'I' and 'My' tell us the narrator is speaking about themselves. This is first person — the narrator IS the storyteller.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word is the ADJECTIVE in this sentence: 'The fluffy kitten slept on the rug.'?
questions.explain: 'Fluffy' is the adjective because it describes what the kitten is like. Adjectives are describing words!

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Replace 'Maria' with the correct pronoun: 'Maria loves art.'
questions.explain: Maria is a girl, so we use the pronoun 'she.' The sentence becomes: 'She loves art.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Choose the right conjunction: 'I like pizza ___ I don't like mushrooms.'
questions.explain: 'But' shows contrast — two opposite ideas. I like pizza (positive) BUT I don't like mushrooms (negative). They are opposites, so we use 'but.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a conjunction correctly?
options: I was tired but I went to sleep.
I was tired I went to sleep.
I was tired or I went to sleep.
I was tired so I went to sleep.
questions.explain: 'So' shows a result. Being tired is the reason, and going to sleep is the result. 'I was tired SO I went to sleep' makes the best sense.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word is an adjective in: 'She carried a heavy bag to school.'?
questions.explain: 'Heavy' is the adjective. It describes the bag — it tells us what KIND of bag it is. Adjectives describe nouns!

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Replace the underlined word with the correct pronoun: 'Carlos and I went to the park.'
questions.explain: 'Carlos and I' refers to two people including the speaker. We use 'we' to replace a group that includes yourself: 'We went to the park.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word has the /oi/ sound (like in 'toy')?
questions.explain: 'Coin' has the /oi/ sound. The letters 'oi' together make the same sound as the 'oy' in 'toy.' c-oi-n = /koin/.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: What vowel sound do you hear in the word 'moon'?
questions.explain: 'Moon' has the /oo/ sound — a long oo like in 'too' and 'food.' The letters 'oo' together make this sound.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: 'ow' can make the /ō/ sound (like in 'snow') or the /ow/ sound (like in 'cow'). Which sound does 'elbow' use?
questions.explain: 'Elbow' uses the /ō/ sound, like 'snow.' Say it: el-bō. The 'ow' at the end says /ō/.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word has the /ou/ sound (like in 'loud')?
questions.explain: 'Cloud' has the /ou/ sound. The letters 'ou' in 'cloud' make the same sound as 'ow' in 'loud.' cl-ou-d = /kloud/.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word has a DIFFERENT vowel sound from the others?
questions.explain: 'Book,' 'cook,' and 'look' all have the short /oo/ sound (like 'foot'). 'Moon' has the long /oo/ sound (like 'food'). Moon is different!

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: The letters 'igh' in 'night' make which sound?
questions.explain: The letters 'igh' together make the long /ī/ sound. Night = /nīt/. Other examples: light, right, tight — they all use 'igh' to say /ī/.

questions.subject: reading
questions.topic: Passage Comprehension — Main Idea and Details
questions.prompt: Read this: 'Water is very important for all living things. People need to drink water every day to stay healthy. Plants use water to grow. Fish and other animals live in water.' Which sentence BEST states the main idea?
options: Water is important for all living things.
questions.explain: The very first sentence says it all: 'Water is very important for all living things.' All the other sentences give examples of this main idea.
questions.passage: Water is very important for all living things. People need to drink water every day to stay healthy. Plants use water to grow. Fish and other animals live in water.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a contraction CORRECTLY?
options: She isn't going to the party.
She is'nt going to the party.
She isnt' going to the party.
She is not' going to the party.
questions.explain: 'Isn't' is the correct contraction for 'is not.' The apostrophe goes where the 'o' is removed: is + not = isn't.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A store had 456 apples. They sold 128 on Monday and 93 on Tuesday. How many apples are left?
questions.explain: Add the apples sold: 128 + 93 = 221. Then subtract from total: 456 − 221 = 235 apples left.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Leo earned $75 in week 1 and $84 in week 2. He spent $46. How much does he have left?
questions.explain: Add Leo's earnings: $75 + $84 = $159. Then subtract what he spent: $159 − $46 = $113.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: There were 312 students at school. 145 went on a field trip. Then 28 more students arrived late. How many students are at school now?
questions.explain: Subtract: 312 − 145 = 167. Then add the late students: 167 + 28 = 195 students.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A baker made 325 muffins. She sold 148 in the morning and 76 in the afternoon. How many muffins were left?
questions.explain: Add the muffins sold: 148 + 76 = 224. Then subtract: 325 − 224 = 101 muffins left.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A jar had 200 marbles. Sam took out 45 and then put back 18. How many marbles are in the jar now?
questions.explain: Subtract: 200 − 45 = 155. Then add back: 155 + 18 = 173 marbles.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A library had 504 books. They got 137 new books on Monday. On Tuesday they removed 89 old books. How many books are there now?
questions.explain: Add new books: 504 + 137 = 641. Then subtract removed books: 641 − 89 = 552 books.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Mia says 348 + 200 = 548. Is she right?
options: Yes, but only if you use a calculator
questions.explain: Mia is right! When you add 200, only the hundreds digit changes: 3 + 2 = 5, so 348 + 200 = 548.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: To solve 605 − 399, which strategy would be EASIEST?
options: Round 399 to 400, subtract, then add 1 back
Use long subtraction column by column
questions.explain: Rounding 399 to 400 makes it easy: 605 − 400 = 205, then add 1 back because we subtracted 1 too many: 205 + 1 = 206.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which number sentence shows the commutative property of addition?
questions.explain: The commutative property means you can switch the order of numbers and the sum stays the same. 5 + 3 = 3 + 5 shows this because both equal 8.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Jake says 7 × 4 = 28. Which strategy could he have used?
questions.explain: To multiply 7 × 4, you can skip-count by 7 exactly 4 times: 7, 14, 21, 28. That gives the correct answer of 28.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Sam wants to add 245 + 300. What is the best way to think about this?
options: Just add 3 to the hundreds digit: 545
questions.explain: Adding 300 only changes the hundreds digit. 2 + 3 = 5, so 245 + 300 = 545. It's the fastest way!

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: School starts at 8:15 AM and ends at 3:00 PM. How long is the school day?
questions.explain: From 8:15 to 3:00: from 8:15 to 9:15 is 1 hour. From 9:15 to 3:00 is 5 hours 45 minutes. Total: 6 hours 45 minutes.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A movie starts at 1:30 PM and lasts 1 hour 45 minutes. When does it end?
questions.explain: Start at 1:30. Add 1 hour: 2:30. Add 45 minutes: 2:30 + 45 minutes = 3:15 PM.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: If you leave at 9:40 AM and arrive at 11:15 AM, how long did the trip take?
questions.explain: From 9:40 to 10:40 is 1 hour. From 10:40 to 11:15 is 35 minutes. Total: 1 hour 35 minutes.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Practice starts at 4:00 PM and lasts 45 minutes. What time does it end?
questions.explain: Start at 4:00 PM and count 45 minutes forward: 4:00 + 45 minutes = 4:45 PM.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Dinner started at 6:15 PM and ended at 7:05 PM. How long did dinner last?
questions.explain: From 6:15 to 7:05: from 6:15 to 7:15 would be 60 minutes, but we stop at 7:05, which is 10 minutes before 7:15. So 60 − 10 = 50 minutes.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: You buy a pencil for $0.37 and pay with $1.00. What is your change?
questions.explain: $1.00 − $0.37 = $0.63. You get 63 cents back in change.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A snack costs $1.85. You pay $2.25. How much change do you get?
questions.explain: $2.25 − $1.85 = $0.40. You get 40 cents back.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: You have 3 quarters, 1 dime, and 2 nickels. How much money is that?
questions.explain: 3 quarters = 75 cents. 1 dime = 10 cents. 2 nickels = 10 cents. 75 + 10 + 10 = $1.00.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A toy costs $3.47. You pay with a $5 bill. How much change should you get?
questions.explain: $5.00 − $3.47 = $1.53. You get $1 and 53 cents back.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A book costs $2.50. You have 1 dollar bill, 6 quarters, and 1 dime. Do you have enough money?
questions.explain: 1 dollar = $1.00. 6 quarters = $1.50. 1 dime = $0.10. Total = $1.00 + $1.50 + $0.10 = $2.60. That's enough to buy the $2.50 book!

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A bookshelf is 85 cm tall. A lamp next to it is 120 cm tall. How much taller is the lamp?
questions.explain: Subtract: 120 − 85 = 35 cm. The lamp is 35 centimeters taller than the bookshelf.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: About how long is a typical classroom?
questions.explain: A typical classroom is about 10 meters long. That's about as long as a big school bus! 2 meters is too short, and 50 or 500 meters would be way too long.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A red ribbon is 47 cm. A blue ribbon is 29 cm. How long are they together?
questions.explain: Add the two lengths: 47 + 29 = 76 cm. Together, the ribbons are 76 centimeters long.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A caterpillar was 3 cm long. It grew 4 more centimeters. Then it grew 2 more. How long is it now?
questions.explain: Start with 3 cm. Add 4: 3 + 4 = 7. Add 2 more: 7 + 2 = 9 cm. The caterpillar is 9 centimeters long.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What unit would you use to measure the length of a swimming pool?
questions.explain: Meters are best for measuring large things like a swimming pool. Centimeters are for smaller things, millimeters are very tiny, and kilograms measure weight not length.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A square is divided into 3 equal parts. What is each part called?
questions.explain: When a shape is divided into 3 equal parts, each part is called one-third, written as 1/3.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which fraction shows 2 out of 4 equal parts shaded?
questions.explain: When 2 out of 4 equal parts are shaded, the fraction is 2/4. The top number (numerator) tells how many parts are shaded, and the bottom (denominator) tells the total parts.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: If you eat 1 of 4 equal slices of pizza, what fraction did you eat?
questions.explain: You ate 1 slice out of 4 total equal slices. That is the fraction 1/4, which means one-fourth of the pizza.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A rectangle is divided into 4 equal parts. 3 parts are shaded blue. Which fraction shows the UNSHADED part?
questions.explain: If 3 out of 4 parts are shaded, then 1 part is NOT shaded. The unshaded fraction is 1/4.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which shape shows halves?
options: A circle cut into 2 equal parts
A circle cut into 3 equal parts
A square cut into 4 equal parts
A triangle cut into 2 unequal parts
questions.explain: Halves means 2 equal parts. Only a circle cut into 2 equal parts shows halves. The parts must be equal in size.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A pictograph shows: ⭐ = 2 votes. Dogs have 4 stars. How many kids voted for dogs?
questions.explain: Each star stands for 2 votes. There are 4 stars, so 4 × 2 = 8 kids voted for dogs.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A bar graph shows: Monday's reading score is 30, Tuesday's is 45. How many MORE points on Tuesday than Monday?
questions.explain: Subtract Monday from Tuesday: 45 − 30 = 15. Tuesday had 15 more points than Monday.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A tally chart shows: Cats = 6 tallies, Dogs = 9 tallies, Birds = 3 tallies. How many animals in all?
questions.explain: Add all the tallies: 6 + 9 + 3 = 18 animals total.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A pictograph shows: 🍎 = 5 apples. Red apples have 3 pictures, green apples have 2 pictures. How many MORE red apples are there?
questions.explain: Red apples: 3 × 5 = 15. Green apples: 2 × 5 = 10. Difference: 15 − 10 = 5 more red apples.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: The pattern is: 5, 10, 15, 20, ___. What comes next?
questions.explain: The rule is add 5 each time: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. Each number is 5 more than the one before it.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: All even numbers can be divided evenly by ___.
questions.explain: Even numbers like 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 can always be divided into groups of 2 with nothing left over. They are all divisible by 2.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which set of numbers follows the rule 'add 7'?
questions.explain: Starting at 4, add 7 each time: 4 + 7 = 11, 11 + 7 = 18, 18 + 7 = 25. The pattern 4, 11, 18, 25 follows the rule 'add 7'.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Is the sum of two odd numbers always odd or even?
questions.explain: When you add two odd numbers, the sum is always even. For example: 3 + 5 = 8, 7 + 9 = 16. Try it — it always works!

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which number is ODD?
questions.explain: A number is odd if it ends in 1, 3, 5, 7, or 9. The number 47 ends in 7, so it is odd. The others end in 8, 6, and 2, so they are even.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is the value of the digit 7 in 726?
questions.explain: In the number 726, the digit 7 is in the hundreds place. That means its value is 7 hundreds, or 700.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Write 534 in expanded form.
questions.explain: Expanded form shows the value of each digit. 5 is in the hundreds place (500), 3 is in the tens place (30), and 4 is in the ones place (4). So 534 = 500 + 30 + 4.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which number is 100 more than 489?
questions.explain: To find 100 more, add 1 to the hundreds digit: 4 + 1 = 5. So 100 more than 489 is 589.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: What is the value of the digit 4 in 847?
questions.explain: In 847, the digit 4 is in the tens place. The tens place means groups of 10, so 4 in the tens place = 40.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which number has a 6 in the tens place?
questions.explain: In 362: 3 is hundreds, 6 is tens, 2 is ones. The digit 6 is in the tens place. In 623, the 6 is in the hundreds place.

questions.subject: math
questions.explain: Put the values together: 3 hundreds, 5 tens, 8 ones = 358. The hundreds digit is 3, tens digit is 5, ones digit is 8.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A farmer had 750 seeds. He planted 246 seeds in Field A and 185 seeds in Field B. How many seeds does he have left?
questions.explain: Add seeds planted: 246 + 185 = 431. Subtract from total: 750 − 431 = 319 seeds left.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A bar graph shows 3 classes read books: Class A = 24, Class B = 36, Class C = 18. How many books did all three classes read together?
questions.explain: Add all three: 24 + 36 + 18. First, 24 + 36 = 60. Then, 60 + 18 = 78 books in all.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Maria started reading at 2:20 PM and read for 55 minutes. What time did she stop?
questions.explain: Start at 2:20 and add 55 minutes. 2:20 + 40 minutes = 3:00. Then add 15 more minutes: 3:00 + 15 = 3:15 PM.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Tyler says 9 + 7 = 7 + 9. What property does this show?
questions.explain: The commutative property says you can switch the order of numbers when adding and the sum stays the same. 9 + 7 = 16 and 7 + 9 = 16 — same answer either way!

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Dolphins are very smart animals. They can learn tricks and even use tools. Scientists have found that dolphins talk to each other using clicks and whistles. Dolphins also help each other when one is sick or hurt.
questions.prompt: What is the MAIN IDEA of this passage?
questions.explain: The main idea is what the whole passage is mostly about. Every sentence in the passage tells us more about how smart dolphins are, so that is the main idea.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Dolphins are very smart animals. They can learn tricks and even use tools. Scientists have found that dolphins talk to each other using clicks and whistles. Dolphins also help each other when one is sick or hurt.
questions.prompt: Which detail from the passage BEST supports the main idea that dolphins are smart?
options: Dolphins talk to each other using clicks and whistles
Dolphins live in groups called pods
questions.explain: Using a special language of clicks and whistles to communicate shows intelligence. This detail best supports the idea that dolphins are smart.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Exercise is important for your body. When you run and play, your heart gets stronger. Exercise also helps your muscles grow big and powerful. Kids who exercise regularly feel happier and sleep better at night.
questions.prompt: What is the MAIN IDEA of this passage?
options: Exercise is important for your body
questions.explain: The main idea is stated in the very first sentence. All the other sentences give details about why exercise is important for your body.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Exercise is important for your body. When you run and play, your heart gets stronger. Exercise also helps your muscles grow big and powerful. Kids who exercise regularly feel happier and sleep better at night.
questions.prompt: Which sentence is a SUPPORTING DETAIL in this passage?
options: Exercise helps your muscles grow big and powerful
Exercise is important for your body
You should eat vegetables every day
Sleep is the most important thing for kids
questions.explain: A supporting detail gives more information about the main idea. 'Exercise helps your muscles grow' is a detail that explains one way exercise helps your body.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Recycling helps protect the Earth. When we recycle, less trash goes to landfills. Recycling saves trees because we use less paper. You can help by sorting your cans, bottles, and paper!
questions.prompt: Why did the author MOST LIKELY write this passage about recycling?
options: To inform readers about how recycling helps the Earth
To entertain readers with a funny recycling story
To confuse readers about what recycling means
To sell recycling bins to readers
questions.explain: The author gives facts about how recycling helps the Earth. When an author shares facts and information, their purpose is to INFORM — to teach readers something.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: A story about a magic dragon who grants wishes is probably written to ___.
options: Entertain readers with an exciting story
Persuade readers to own a dragon
questions.explain: A story about a magic dragon is fiction — it is made up. Stories that are made up are usually written to ENTERTAIN, meaning to be fun and exciting to read.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: You MUST buy Crunch-O cereal! It is the most delicious cereal ever made. Every bite is crispy and sweet. Don't miss out — buy Crunch-O today!
questions.prompt: What is the author's purpose for writing this?
options: To persuade you to buy the cereal
To inform you about cereal ingredients
To entertain you with a funny cereal story
To explain how cereal is made
questions.explain: Words like 'You MUST buy' and 'Don't miss out' are trying to convince you to do something. When a writer tries to convince you, the purpose is to PERSUADE.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: You MUST buy Crunch-O cereal! It is the most delicious cereal ever made. Every bite is crispy and sweet. Don't miss out — buy Crunch-O today!
questions.prompt: Which word in the passage MOST shows the author wants to PERSUADE you?
questions.explain: The word 'MUST' tells you that the author is ordering you or strongly urging you to do something. This is a persuasive word used to convince the reader.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: What does a CAPTION below a photo tell you?
options: It explains what is shown in the photo
It tells you the name of the author
It gives the page number of the chapter
It shows the table of contents
questions.explain: A caption is a short sentence or phrase printed below or next to a photo. It explains what is happening in the picture or gives more information about it.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: You want to quickly find information in chapter 3. Which text feature do you use?
questions.explain: A table of contents is at the front of a book and lists all the chapters and their page numbers. You can use it to jump quickly to chapter 3.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Bold words in a textbook usually mean ___.
questions.explain: Bold words are printed darker and thicker than normal words. Authors use bold to highlight important vocabulary or key terms that students should pay attention to.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Where would you look to find the definition of the word 'habitat' in a science textbook?
questions.explain: A glossary is in the back of the book and lists important words with their definitions. It is like a mini-dictionary just for that book.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: A nonfiction book has headings like 'Life Cycle' and 'Habitat.' What do these headings tell you?
options: They show the topic of each section
They are the title of the book
They tell you the author's name
questions.explain: Headings are titles for each section of a nonfiction text. They tell the reader what that part of the text will be about, so you can find information quickly.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: The prefix 'un-' in the word 'unhappy' means ___.
questions.explain: The prefix 'un-' means 'not.' So 'unhappy' means 'not happy.' Other examples: unlock = not locked, undo = not done.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Add '-ful' to the word 'care.' What does 'careful' mean?
options: Full of care; paying close attention
questions.explain: The suffix '-ful' means 'full of.' So 'careful' means 'full of care' — paying close attention so you don't make mistakes or get hurt.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: If 're-' means 'again,' what does 'rewrite' mean?
questions.explain: The prefix 're-' means 'again.' So 'rewrite' means 'to write again.' If your teacher asks you to rewrite your essay, you write it one more time.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: What does the word 'helpless' mean?
questions.explain: The suffix '-less' means 'without.' So 'helpless' means 'without help' — not able to help yourself or be helped.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word means 'not safe'?
questions.explain: The prefix 'un-' means 'not.' Adding 'un-' to 'safe' gives us 'unsafe,' which means 'not safe.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: The exhausted runner collapsed after the long race. She had been running for three hours.
questions.prompt: In this sentence, what does EXHAUSTED most likely mean?
questions.explain: The clues 'collapsed' and 'running for three hours' tell us the runner had no energy left. EXHAUSTED means extremely tired.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: The parched hiker drank the entire bottle of water in one gulp.
questions.prompt: Use context clues: what does PARCHED most likely mean?
questions.explain: The clue is that the hiker 'drank the entire bottle of water.' That tells us they really needed water — they were PARCHED, which means very thirsty.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: The tiny kitten was trembling in the corner of the cold, dark room.
questions.prompt: What does TREMBLING most likely mean in this sentence?
questions.explain: The clues 'cold' and 'dark room' help us understand the kitten was scared or cold. TREMBLING means shaking, which happens when you are cold or frightened.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: The ancient tree had been growing in the forest for over five hundred years.
questions.prompt: What does ANCIENT most likely mean?
questions.explain: The clue 'five hundred years' tells us the tree has been there for a very long time. ANCIENT means very, very old.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Mia was beaming with joy when she won first place at the science fair.
questions.prompt: What does BEAMING most likely mean?
questions.explain: The clue 'joy' tells us Mia was very happy. BEAMING means smiling very brightly because you are extremely happy.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage:
Passage A: Sharks have sharp teeth and powerful tails. They are excellent hunters. Most sharks live in salty ocean water. Sharks must keep swimming or they will sink.

Passage B: Sharks come in many sizes. The whale shark is the biggest fish in the ocean. Even though sharks look scary, most sharks do not attack people. Sharks are important to keep ocean life balanced.
questions.prompt: What do BOTH passages say about sharks?
options: Sharks must keep swimming or sink
Sharks are important to the ocean
questions.explain: Both passages talk about sharks in the ocean. Passage A says 'most sharks live in salty ocean water' and Passage B talks about ocean life. The ocean is mentioned in both.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage:
Passage A: Sharks have sharp teeth and powerful tails. They are excellent hunters. Most sharks live in salty ocean water. Sharks must keep swimming or they will sink.

Passage B: Sharks come in many sizes. The whale shark is the biggest fish in the ocean. Even though sharks look scary, most sharks do not attack people. Sharks are important to keep ocean life balanced.
questions.prompt: How are the two passages DIFFERENT?
options: Passage A focuses on how sharks hunt; Passage B focuses on shark size and safety
Passage A says sharks are safe; Passage B says they are dangerous
Passage A is about whale sharks; Passage B is about great white sharks
Both passages give the same information
questions.explain: Passage A tells us how sharks hunt and move. Passage B tells us about shark size and that most sharks don't attack people. They each give different kinds of information.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage:
Passage A: Bees collect pollen from flowers. They bring it back to their hive. Bees make honey by turning the nectar from flowers into a sweet, thick liquid.

Passage B: Bees are very important to farmers. When bees visit flowers, they help plants grow fruit and seeds. Without bees, we would have far fewer fruits and vegetables to eat.
questions.prompt: What topic do BOTH passages share?
questions.explain: Both passages mention bees visiting flowers. Passage A talks about bees collecting pollen and nectar from flowers. Passage B talks about bees helping plants that grow from flowers.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the CORRECT past tense?
options: He ran home as fast as he could.
He runned home as fast as he could.
He runed home as fast as he could.
He ranned home as fast as he could.
questions.explain: The word 'run' is an irregular verb. Its past tense is 'ran,' not 'runned' or 'runed.' Irregular verbs have special past tense forms you have to memorize.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: What is the plural of 'tooth'?
questions.explain: 'Tooth' is an irregular noun. Its plural is 'teeth,' not 'tooths.' Some nouns change their spelling completely when there is more than one.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Yesterday she ___ to the park with her dog.
questions.explain: The word 'go' is an irregular verb. Its past tense is 'went,' not 'goed.' Since this happened yesterday, we need the past tense form.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence is CORRECT?
options: The children ate their lunch quickly.
The childrens ate their lunch quickly.
The childs ate their lunch quickly.
The childen ate their lunch quickly.
questions.explain: 'Child' has an irregular plural: 'children,' not 'childs' or 'childrens.' The sentence 'The children ate their lunch' is correct.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: Last night, the puppy ___ under the bed.
questions.explain: The past tense of 'hide' is 'hid.' It is an irregular verb, so we do not add '-ed.' We say 'he hid' not 'he hided.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word is an ADVERB in: 'The dog ran quickly across the yard'?
questions.explain: An adverb describes how, when, or where something happens. 'Quickly' tells us HOW the dog ran. Adverbs often end in '-ly.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which adjective makes this sentence more PRECISE? 'She carried a ___ box down the stairs.'
questions.explain: A precise adjective gives a clear, specific picture. 'Heavy' tells exactly what kind of box it was. Words like 'nice,' 'good,' and 'okay' are too vague to paint a clear picture.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word is an ADJECTIVE in: 'The fluffy kitten purred softly on the warm blanket'?
questions.explain: An adjective describes a noun. 'Fluffy' describes the kitten (a noun), so it is an adjective. 'Softly' is an adverb describing how the kitten purred.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses an adverb to improve 'The bird sang'?
questions.explain: 'Sweetly' is an adverb that tells HOW the bird sang. Adding 'sweetly' makes the sentence more interesting and detailed. Adverbs often end in '-ly.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which of these is an ADVERB?
questions.explain: 'Slowly' is an adverb because it describes HOW something is done. It ends in '-ly,' which is a clue that it is an adverb. 'Mountain' is a noun, 'Purple' is an adjective, and 'Jump' is a verb.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Maya wanted to bake cookies, but she had no eggs. She looked all around the kitchen. Then she remembered that her neighbor always had extra eggs. Maya knocked on her neighbor's door, and the neighbor smiled and gave her two eggs. Maya baked the most delicious cookies ever!
questions.prompt: What is the PROBLEM in this story?
options: Maya had no eggs to bake cookies
Maya did not know how to bake
questions.explain: The problem is what makes things difficult for the character. Maya wanted to bake cookies but had no eggs — that is the main problem in the story.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Maya wanted to bake cookies, but she had no eggs. She looked all around the kitchen. Then she remembered that her neighbor always had extra eggs. Maya knocked on her neighbor's door, and the neighbor smiled and gave her two eggs. Maya baked the most delicious cookies ever!
questions.prompt: How did Maya SOLVE her problem?
options: She got eggs from her neighbor
She used flour instead of eggs
She bought eggs at the store
She decided not to make cookies
questions.explain: Maya solved her problem by asking her neighbor for eggs. The neighbor gave her two eggs, and Maya was able to bake her cookies.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: On Monday, Carlos lost his library book. He looked under his bed and in his backpack. He felt terrible. On Tuesday, his mom found the book inside the laundry basket. Carlos was so relieved. He returned the book and got a new one.
questions.prompt: What happened FIRST in this story?
questions.explain: Story events happen in order. The very first thing that happened was Carlos lost his library book — that started everything else in the story.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: On Monday, Carlos lost his library book. He looked under his bed and in his backpack. He felt terrible. On Tuesday, his mom found the book inside the laundry basket. Carlos was so relieved. He returned the book and got a new one.
questions.prompt: What is the SOLUTION to Carlos's problem?
options: His mom found the book in the laundry basket
He bought a new library book
He told the librarian he lost it
He found it under his bed
questions.explain: The solution is how the problem is fixed. Carlos's mom found the lost book in the laundry basket. That solved the problem of the missing library book.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Frogs go through big changes as they grow up. A frog starts as a tiny egg in a pond. The egg hatches into a tadpole that swims with its tail. Slowly, the tadpole grows legs and loses its tail. Finally, it becomes a frog that can live on land and in water.
questions.prompt: What is the MAIN IDEA of this passage?
options: Frogs go through big changes as they grow up
Frogs can live on land and in water
questions.explain: The main idea is stated in the very first sentence. Every other sentence describes one of the changes a frog goes through — they all support that main idea.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Did you know that cleaning your room can make you feel better? When your room is messy, it can be hard to find things. A clean room helps you think clearly and feel calm. Try cleaning your room today — you might be surprised how good it feels!
questions.prompt: What is the author's purpose in this passage?
options: To persuade you to clean your room
To tell a funny story about a messy room
To teach you how rooms are built
To explain the history of bedrooms
questions.explain: The author uses phrases like 'Try cleaning your room today' to convince the reader to do something. That is a persuasive purpose — trying to get you to agree and act.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: What does the word 'painless' mean?
questions.explain: The suffix '-less' means 'without.' So 'painless' means without pain. A painless shot is one that doesn't hurt at all.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: The enormous elephant splashed water on itself to cool down in the hot sun.
questions.prompt: What does ENORMOUS most likely mean?
questions.explain: We know elephants are one of the biggest animals in the world. The word ENORMOUS describes something very, very big. It is used here to describe the elephant's great size.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: What is the plural of 'mouse'?
questions.explain: 'Mouse' is an irregular noun. Its plural form is 'mice,' not 'mouses.' Irregular plurals change their spelling instead of just adding '-s.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Lily's kite got stuck high up in a tree. She tried jumping to reach it but couldn't. She asked her dad for help. Her dad got a long ladder from the garage and climbed up to get the kite down. Lily thanked her dad and flew her kite happily the rest of the afternoon.
questions.prompt: What is the PROBLEM in this story?
options: Lily's kite got stuck in a tree
Lily did not know how to fly a kite
Lily's dad was too busy to help
questions.explain: The problem is the challenge the character faces. Lily's kite being stuck in a tree is what causes trouble and drives the whole story.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage:
Passage A: The sun is a giant star made of hot gases. It gives Earth light and warmth. Without the sun, no plants could grow.

Passage B: The sun rises in the east every morning and sets in the west every evening. The sun's position in the sky changes with the seasons. In summer, the sun is higher in the sky.
questions.prompt: What do BOTH passages talk about?
questions.explain: Both passages are about the sun. Passage A describes what the sun is made of, and Passage B describes how the sun moves in the sky. The shared topic is the sun.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: A nonfiction book has a map of the United States on page 14. Below the map is the sentence: 'The shaded states get the most rain.' This sentence is called a ___.
questions.explain: A caption is a sentence written below or next to a picture, map, or diagram that explains what it shows. 'The shaded states get the most rain' is a caption for the map.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses an adjective AND an adverb correctly?
options: The tiny turtle walked slowly to the pond.
The turtle walked tiny slowly to the pond.
Slowly tiny turtle walked to the pond.
The turtle tiny walked to the slow pond.
questions.explain: 'Tiny' is an adjective that describes the turtle (a noun). 'Slowly' is an adverb that describes how the turtle walked. Both are used correctly in the first sentence.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Bees are amazing insects that help our world. They fly from flower to flower collecting nectar. This helps plants grow fruit and seeds. Bees also make honey, which people have eaten for thousands of years. If bees disappeared, many foods we love would disappear too.
questions.prompt: Which sentence is a supporting detail — NOT the main idea?
options: Bees fly from flower to flower collecting nectar.
Bees are amazing insects that help our world.
Bees are very important to plants and people.
Bees do many helpful things for our planet.
questions.explain: A supporting detail gives a specific example or fact. 'Bees fly from flower to flower collecting nectar' is a specific fact about what bees do — it supports the bigger idea that bees are amazing and helpful.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A class has 4 tables with 6 students at each table. If 5 students were absent, how many students were present?
questions.explain: Step 1: Total students = 4 × 6 = 24. Step 2: Students present = 24 − 5 = 19.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A baker makes 8 batches of 12 cookies each. She sells 37 cookies. How many cookies does she have left?
questions.explain: Step 1: Total cookies = 8 × 12 = 96. Step 2: Cookies left = 96 − 37 = 59.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A ribbon is 96 cm long. It is cut into pieces 8 cm each. If 3 pieces are used, how many pieces remain?
questions.explain: Step 1: Total pieces = 96 ÷ 8 = 12. Step 2: Pieces remaining = 12 − 3 = 9.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Sam has 5 bags with 9 marbles each. He gives away 12 marbles. How many marbles does he have now?
questions.explain: Step 1: Total marbles = 5 × 9 = 45. Step 2: Marbles left = 45 − 12 = 33.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A store has 7 shelves. Each shelf holds 8 books. A delivery adds 15 more books and they fill evenly across 5 shelves. How many books total are on those 5 shelves after adding?
questions.explain: Step 1: Books on 5 shelves before delivery = 5 × 8 = 40. Step 2: Each of the 5 shelves gets 15 ÷ 5 = 3 more books. Step 3: Total = 40 + 15 = 43 books across those 5 shelves.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: There are 6 teams. Each team has 7 players. After the game, 8 players went home early. How many players were still there?
questions.explain: Step 1: Total players = 6 × 7 = 42. Step 2: Players still there = 42 − 8 = 34.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Maya earns $9 per hour. She works for 6 hours on Saturday and 4 hours on Sunday. She spends $35 on a gift. How much money does she have left?
questions.explain: Step 1: Total hours = 6 + 4 = 10. Step 2: Total earned = 10 × $9 = $90. Step 3: Money left = $90 − $35 = $55.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which fraction is closer to 1 whole: 5/6 or 3/8?
questions.explain: 5/6 is very close to 1 (only 1/6 away). 3/8 is less than halfway to 1. So 5/6 is closer to 1 whole.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Order these fractions from LEAST to GREATEST: 1/4, 3/4, 1/2
questions.explain: 1/4 is the smallest (25%). 1/2 is next (50%). 3/4 is the largest (75%). So the order is 1/4, 1/2, 3/4.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which fraction is greater: 5/8 or 5/12? How do you know?
options: 5/8, because the pieces are larger when there are fewer pieces
They are equal because the numerators are the same
5/12, because more pieces means more total
questions.explain: Both fractions have 5 pieces. When the denominator is smaller (8 vs 12), each piece is bigger. So 5/8 has 5 larger pieces, making it greater than 5/12.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which fraction is LESS than 1/2?
questions.explain: 1/2 = 4/8. Since 3/8 is less than 4/8, it is less than 1/2. The others are all greater than 1/2.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Lisa says 2/3 is greater than 3/4 because 2 and 3 are smaller numbers than 3 and 4. Is she correct?
options: Yes — smaller numbers mean bigger fractions
questions.explain: Lisa is wrong. 3/4 = 0.75 and 2/3 ≈ 0.67, so 3/4 is greater. You cannot compare fractions just by looking at the size of the numbers.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which fraction is equivalent to 2/4?
questions.explain: 2/4 simplifies to 1/2 because both 2 and 4 can be divided by 2. So 1/2 is equivalent to 2/4.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 1/3 = __/9
questions.explain: To go from 3 to 9, multiply by 3. Do the same to the numerator: 1 × 3 = 3. So 1/3 = 3/9.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Marcus says 3/6 and 1/2 are the same amount. Is he correct?
options: No — 3 and 6 are different from 1 and 2
Yes — but only when the denominators match
questions.explain: Marcus is correct! Divide both 3 and 6 by 3: 3÷3 = 1 and 6÷3 = 2. So 3/6 = 1/2. They name the same amount.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which fraction is NOT equivalent to 2/3?
questions.explain: 3/6 simplifies to 1/2, not 2/3. The fractions 4/6, 6/9, and 8/12 all simplify to 2/3.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which two fractions are equivalent? 2/5 and 4/10, or 2/5 and 3/10?
questions.explain: 2/5: multiply top and bottom by 2 → 4/10. So 2/5 = 4/10. Check 3/10: 2/5 would need 4/10, not 3/10. So only the first pair is equivalent.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A shape is made of two rectangles. One is 4 cm × 3 cm and the other is 2 cm × 5 cm. What is the total area?
questions.explain: Area of first rectangle = 4 × 3 = 12 sq cm. Area of second rectangle = 2 × 5 = 10 sq cm. Total area = 12 + 10 = 22 sq cm.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A room is 6 m long and 4 m wide, but there is a 1 m × 2 m closet cut out of one corner. What is the floor area of the room (not including the closet)?
questions.explain: Total room area = 6 × 4 = 24 sq m. Closet area = 1 × 2 = 2 sq m. Floor area = 24 − 2 = 22 sq m.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: An L-shaped figure can be split into a 5 × 2 rectangle and a 3 × 3 rectangle. What is the total area?
questions.explain: Area of 5 × 2 = 10 sq units. Area of 3 × 3 = 9 sq units. Total = 10 + 9 = 19 sq units.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A garden is shaped like a large rectangle (8 m × 5 m) with a small square (2 m × 2 m) pond in the middle removed. What is the planting area?
questions.explain: Large rectangle area = 8 × 5 = 40 sq m. Pond area = 2 × 2 = 4 sq m. Planting area = 40 − 4 = 36 sq m.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A rectangle has a perimeter of 28 cm. One side is 8 cm long. What is the length of the OTHER (shorter) side?
questions.explain: Perimeter = 2 × (length + width). 28 = 2 × (8 + w). 14 = 8 + w. w = 14 − 8 = 6 cm.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A pentagon has four equal sides of 5 cm each. The total perimeter is 27 cm. What is the length of the fifth side?
questions.explain: The four equal sides add up to 4 × 5 = 20 cm. The fifth side = 27 − 20 = 7 cm.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A square has a perimeter of 36 cm. What is the length of one side?
questions.explain: A square has 4 equal sides. Side = 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A hexagon has five sides that measure 4 cm, 6 cm, 3 cm, 5 cm, and 4 cm. The perimeter is 30 cm. What is the missing sixth side?
questions.explain: Add the known sides: 4 + 6 + 3 + 5 + 4 = 22 cm. Sixth side = 30 − 22 = 8 cm.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A school has 387 students. Round this to the nearest hundred.
questions.explain: 387 is between 300 and 400. The tens digit is 8, which is 5 or more, so round up to 400.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: You have $264. You want to round to the nearest $10 to estimate. About how much money do you have?
questions.explain: 264 is between 260 and 270. The ones digit is 4, which is less than 5, so round down to $260.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A store sold 358 items on Friday and 242 items on Saturday. Rounding each number to the nearest hundred, what is the estimated total?
questions.explain: 358 rounds to 400 (tens digit is 5, round up). 242 rounds to 200 (tens digit is 4, round down). Estimated total = 400 + 200 = 600.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: The number of teachers at a school is 42. Round to the nearest ten. The number of students is 387. Round to the nearest hundred. What are the two rounded values?
questions.explain: 42 rounds to 40 (ones digit is 2, round down). 387 rounds to 400 (tens digit is 8, round up). The rounded values are 40 and 400.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Use the distributive property to solve 7 × 13: (7 × 10) + (7 × __) = ?
questions.explain: 7 × 13 = (7 × 10) + (7 × 3) = 70 + 21 = 91. The missing number is 3, and the answer is 91.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which equation correctly shows the distributive property for 6 × 8?
questions.explain: 6 × 8 = 6 × (5 + 3) = (6 × 5) + (6 × 3) = 30 + 18 = 48. This shows the distributive property correctly.

questions.subject: math
options: Because you multiply 4 by each number inside the parentheses
Because addition and multiplication always give the same answer
Because 5 + 3 = 8 and 4 × 8 is the same as 4 + 8
Because you can change the order of multiplication
questions.explain: The distributive property says you can multiply 4 by each addend separately: 4 × 5 = 20 and 4 × 3 = 12, then add: 20 + 12 = 32. And 4 × (5+3) = 4 × 8 = 32. Same answer!

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Use the distributive property to find 8 × 14.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A play started at 2:15 PM and lasted 1 hour 40 minutes. What time did it end?
questions.explain: Start at 2:15. Add 1 hour → 3:15. Add 40 minutes → 3:55 PM.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Pedro arrived at the library at 10:27 AM and left at 12:05 PM. How long was he there?
questions.explain: From 10:27 to 12:05: 10:27 → 11:27 is 1 hour, then 11:27 → 12:05 is 38 minutes. Total = 1 hour 38 minutes.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: It takes 45 minutes to drive to grandma's house. You leave at 3:50 PM. When do you arrive?
questions.explain: 3:50 + 45 minutes: 3:50 + 10 min = 4:00, then + 35 more min = 4:35 PM.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: School starts at 8:05 AM. Math class begins 35 minutes after school starts and lasts 55 minutes. When does math class end?
questions.explain: School starts at 8:05. Math begins 35 min later: 8:05 + 35 min = 8:40 AM. Math ends 55 min later: 8:40 + 55 min = 9:35 AM.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A movie starts at 6:15 PM and ends at 8:03 PM. How long is the movie?
questions.explain: 6:15 to 8:15 is 2 hours, but end time is 8:03, which is 12 minutes before 8:15. So 2 hours − 12 minutes = 1 hour 48 minutes.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Point A is at 3/8 on a number line from 0 to 1. Which description is correct?
questions.explain: 1/2 = 4/8. Since 3/8 is less than 4/8, point A is between 0 and 1/2.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: On a number line from 0 to 1, where would 2/3 be placed relative to 1/2?
questions.explain: 2/3 ≈ 0.67 and 1/2 = 0.50. Since 0.67 > 0.50, the point 2/3 is to the right of 1/2, closer to 1.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which fraction would be placed at the exact MIDDLE of a number line from 0 to 1?
questions.explain: The middle of a number line from 0 to 1 is 1/2, since it is exactly halfway between 0 and 1.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A number line from 0 to 1 is divided into 6 equal parts. Each part is labeled. What fraction is at the 4th mark?
questions.explain: When a number line from 0 to 1 is divided into 6 equal parts, each mark represents 1/6. The 4th mark is at 4/6.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A farmer has 9 rows of apple trees with 7 trees in each row. Each tree gives 15 apples. The farmer uses 48 apples for pies and sells the rest in bags of 9. How many FULL bags can he make?
questions.explain: Step 1: Total trees = 9 × 7 = 63. Step 2: Total apples = 63 × 15 = 945. Step 3: Apples to sell = 945 − 48 = 897. Step 4: Full bags = 897 ÷ 9 = 99 bags (with 6 left over).

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A T-shaped figure is made by placing a 6 × 2 rectangle on top of a 4 × 4 rectangle. What is the total area?
questions.explain: Area of 6 × 2 rectangle = 12 sq units. Area of 4 × 4 rectangle = 16 sq units. Total area = 12 + 16 = 28 sq units.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which expression equals 9 × 12 using the distributive property?
questions.explain: 9 × 12 = 9 × (10 + 2) = (9 × 10) + (9 × 2) = 90 + 18 = 108. This is the distributive property.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: A rectangle has a perimeter of 50 cm. The length is 4 times the width. What is the width?
questions.explain: Perimeter = 2 × (length + width). Let width = w. Length = 4w. 50 = 2 × (4w + w) = 2 × 5w = 10w. w = 50 ÷ 10 = 5 cm.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Which of the following numbers rounds to 500 when rounded to the nearest hundred?
questions.explain: 482 is between 400 and 500. The tens digit is 8, which is ≥ 5, so we round up to 500. 449 rounds to 400. 350 rounds to 400 (or 400, as it is exactly halfway). 551 rounds to 600.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Jake ran 2/4 of a mile. Anna ran 3/6 of a mile. Who ran farther?
questions.explain: 2/4 = 1/2 (divide by 2). 3/6 = 1/2 (divide by 3). Both fractions equal 1/2, so they ran the same distance.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: On a number line from 0 to 1, which fraction is closest to 0?
questions.explain: 1/8 = 0.125, which is the smallest of the four fractions. It is closest to 0 on the number line.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: There are 3 boxes of crayons. Each box has 24 crayons. The teacher divides them equally among 8 students. Each student uses 4 crayons in art class. How many crayons does each student have left?
questions.explain: Step 1: Total crayons = 3 × 24 = 72. Step 2: Crayons per student = 72 ÷ 8 = 9. Step 3: Crayons left = 9 − 4 = 5.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Mia walked slowly to the front of the classroom. She kept looking at her shoes. When the teacher called her name again, her hands shook slightly as she held her paper.
questions.prompt: What can you INFER about how Mia feels?
questions.explain: The clues — walking slowly, looking at her shoes, and shaking hands — all suggest nervousness. The author shows this through Mia's actions instead of saying 'Mia was nervous.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Marcus always arrived at practice early to set up the equipment. He stayed late to help the coach put everything away. On game day, he memorized every player's name on the opposing team.
questions.prompt: What can you INFER about Marcus from this passage?
options: Marcus wants to be a coach
Marcus does not like his teammates
questions.explain: Marcus arrives early, stays late, and studies the other team. These details show he is dedicated and hardworking. The author doesn't say this directly — you have to infer it from his actions.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Every time Grandma entered the room, the dog ran to her and wagged its tail. When she left, the dog sat by the door and whined softly for several minutes.
questions.prompt: Which sentence from the passage IMPLIES that the dog missed Grandma when she left?
options: The dog sat by the door and whined softly
Every time Grandma entered the room, the dog ran to her
questions.explain: Sitting by the door and whining after Grandma left implies the dog missed her. The author shows the dog's feelings through behavior, not by stating the dog was sad.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Tom opened his lunchbox and stared inside. He slowly closed it. He looked out the window for the rest of lunch without eating anything.
questions.prompt: Which is the BEST inference about why Tom did not eat his lunch?
options: He did not like what was in his lunchbox
He forgot to bring a lunch
He was not hungry because he ate a big breakfast
questions.explain: Tom opened his lunchbox, stared, and closed it without eating. This suggests he didn't like what he saw. While watching outside is mentioned, it was likely a result of not wanting to eat.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Leo wanted to give up when he fell off his bike for the third time. His dad said, 'Every expert was once a beginner.' Leo got back on and practiced every day. By the end of the week, he could ride without holding on.
questions.prompt: What is the THEME of this story?
options: Keep trying and you will improve
questions.explain: Leo kept trying after falling and eventually succeeded. The story's theme is about persistence — keep trying and you will get better.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Emma saw her classmate sitting alone at lunch. She thought about walking past, but remembered how lonely she felt when she was new. Emma sat down and said hello. Soon, others joined them. Her classmate smiled for the first time all week.
questions.prompt: Which sentence from the story BEST supports the theme 'Small acts of kindness can change someone's day'?
options: Her classmate smiled for the first time all week
Emma saw her classmate sitting alone at lunch
She remembered how lonely she felt when she was new
questions.explain: The classmate smiling for the first time all week shows the impact of Emma's small kind act. This is the strongest evidence that one kind gesture can make a big difference.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: When the river flooded, neighbors piled sandbags together all night. People shared food, blankets, and tools. Nobody asked for a reward. When the water receded, the mayor said the town's true strength was its people.
questions.prompt: The author repeats the idea of neighbors working together to develop the theme of ___.
questions.explain: Every detail — sandbags, sharing food, no reward, and the mayor's speech — points to the theme that a community is strongest when people work together.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: What does the simile 'She ran like the wind' mean?
options: She ran outside in the wind
She ran quietly like a breeze
questions.explain: A simile uses 'like' or 'as' to compare two things. 'Like the wind' compares the girl's speed to wind — meaning she ran very fast.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Identify the METAPHOR in this sentence: 'The classroom was a zoo after recess.'
questions.explain: A metaphor says one thing IS another. Saying the classroom 'was a zoo' means it was wild and noisy — like a zoo — without using 'like' or 'as.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: The phrase 'the sun smiled down on us' is an example of what type of figurative language?
questions.explain: Personification gives human qualities to non-human things. The sun cannot actually smile — the author gives it a human action to make the description more vivid.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence contains a SIMILE?
options: His backpack was as heavy as a boulder
The wind whispered through the trees
The test was a mountain to climb
questions.explain: A simile uses 'as' or 'like' to compare. 'As heavy as a boulder' uses 'as' to compare the backpack's weight. The other sentences use personification or metaphor.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: In the sentence 'The old car coughed and sputtered down the road,' what technique does the author use?
questions.explain: The author gives the car a human action ('coughed') — this is personification. Cars don't actually cough; the author uses this word to describe the car's sounds vividly.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage:
Passage 1: Wolves are important predators that help keep deer populations balanced. Without wolves, deer herds grow too large and eat all the plants. Studies in Yellowstone show that wolves helped the whole ecosystem recover.

Passage 2: Wolves can be dangerous to livestock on farms near wilderness areas. Many ranchers report losing sheep and cattle to wolf attacks. Some argue that wolves should be kept in wildlife preserves, away from farmland.
questions.prompt: How does Author 1 DIFFER from Author 2 in their view of wolves?
options: Author 1 sees wolves as beneficial; Author 2 sees them as harmful to farmers
Both authors agree wolves should be protected
Author 2 supports wolves more than Author 1
Both authors think wolves are dangerous
questions.explain: Author 1 focuses on wolves helping ecosystems. Author 2 focuses on the problems wolves cause for farmers. They have opposite views on whether wolves are helpful or harmful.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage:
Passage 1: Bees are responsible for pollinating one-third of the world's food supply. Without bees, many fruits and vegetables would not grow.

Passage 2: Some bee species can be aggressive and sting people, especially near their hives. Bee stings can cause serious allergic reactions in some individuals. It is important to be careful around beehives.
questions.prompt: What information does ONLY Passage 2 include?
options: Bee stings can cause allergic reactions
Bees are important to the world
questions.explain: Only Passage 2 mentions bee stings and allergic reactions. Passage 1 only discusses bees' role in food production.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage:
Passage 1: Exercise is one of the best ways to stay healthy. Running, swimming, and biking strengthen your heart and muscles.

Passage 2: Sleep is essential for good health. Children who get enough sleep do better in school and have stronger immune systems.
questions.prompt: What do BOTH passages agree on?
options: Good habits lead to better health
Sleep is more important than exercise
questions.explain: Passage 1 says exercise helps health, and Passage 2 says sleep helps health. Both agree that healthy habits — whether exercise or sleep — improve your wellbeing.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: The root 'bio-' means life. What does 'biography' most likely mean?
options: A written story of someone's life
A science experiment with living things
A picture of a living thing
questions.explain: 'Bio' means life and 'graphy' means writing. So a biography is a written account of someone's life.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: The suffix '-ology' means 'the study of.' What is 'geology'?
options: The study of the Earth and rocks
questions.explain: 'Geo' means Earth, and '-ology' means the study of. So geology is the study of the Earth and its rocks.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: The prefix 'tri-' means three. How many wheels does a tricycle have?
questions.explain: 'Tri-' means three, and 'cycle' means wheel or circle. So a tricycle has three wheels.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: The root 'port' means 'carry.' Which word means to carry something OUT of a country?
questions.explain: 'Ex-' means out, and 'port' means carry. Export means to carry goods out of a country. Import means to bring in, transport means to carry across, and support means to hold up.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: The root 'aqua' means water. Which word most likely refers to a place where water animals live on display?
questions.explain: An aquarium is a tank or building where water animals are kept and displayed. 'Aqua' (water) + '-arium' (a place for) = aquarium.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: The prefix 'un-' means 'not.' What does 'unhappy' mean?
questions.explain: 'Un-' means not. Unhappy = not happy. Knowing roots and prefixes helps you figure out word meanings.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence is CORRECT?
options: The team is winning the game.
The team are winning the game.
The team were winning the game.
The team be winning the game.
questions.explain: When 'team' refers to one group acting together, it is singular and takes the singular verb 'is.' 'The team is winning' is correct.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: 'Neither the cat nor the dogs ___ the food.'
questions.explain: When using 'neither...nor,' the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. 'Dogs' is plural and closest to the verb, so we use 'want.' The sentence is: Neither the cat nor the dogs want the food.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Choose the correct pronoun: 'Each of the students turned in ___ homework.'
questions.explain: 'Each' is singular, so it needs a singular pronoun. 'His or her' is the formally correct singular pronoun. 'Their' is increasingly accepted but 'his or her' is the traditional grammar rule for this usage.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence has CORRECT subject-verb agreement?
options: The dogs run in the park every morning.
The dogs runs in the park every morning.
The dogs is running in the park every morning.
The dogs be running in the park every morning.
questions.explain: 'Dogs' is plural, so it uses the plural verb 'run.' We do not add -s to the verb with a plural subject.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb to complete the sentence: 'The birds in the tree ___ very loudly.'
questions.explain: 'Birds' is plural, so the verb should be 'sing' (no -s). 'Sings' is for a singular subject like 'the bird sings.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: The word 'bark' has two meanings. Which meaning is used in: 'She scraped her knee on the rough bark of the oak'?
options: The outer covering of a tree
questions.explain: In this sentence, 'bark' refers to the rough outer covering of a tree (the oak). Context clues like 'rough' and 'oak' help us figure out the right meaning.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word has a MORE POSITIVE connotation: stubborn or determined?
questions.explain: 'Determined' suggests strength and focus in a positive way. 'Stubborn' usually means refusing to change — which has a more negative tone. Both describe not giving up, but 'determined' is seen more positively.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: The word 'ancient' means very old. What additional idea does it suggest beyond just 'old'?
options: Something from long, long ago — often important or mysterious
Something that is exactly 100 years old
questions.explain: 'Ancient' means extremely old — often from thousands of years ago. It often suggests something historically important, mysterious, or remarkable, unlike the plain word 'old.'

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read: 'She wandered through the store.' Which word could REPLACE 'wandered' while keeping the same meaning?
questions.explain: 'Wandered' means to walk slowly without a clear direction. 'Strolled' also means to walk slowly and casually — it keeps the same meaning. Sprinting, marching, and dashing all suggest fast or purposeful movement.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which word has a NEGATIVE connotation when describing a person's strong belief?
questions.explain: 'Fanatic' suggests someone whose belief is extreme and unreasonable — it has a negative tone. 'Devoted,' 'passionate,' and 'committed' are all more positive ways to describe strong belief.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: First, the caterpillar hatches from an egg. Next, it eats leaves and grows larger. Then, it forms a chrysalis. Finally, a beautiful butterfly emerges from the chrysalis.
questions.prompt: What text structure does this passage use?
questions.explain: The words 'First,' 'Next,' 'Then,' and 'Finally' signal chronological (time) order. The passage tells the stages of a butterfly's life in order.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Many cities have too much trash filling their landfills. One solution is recycling programs that turn old materials into new products. Another solution is composting food waste instead of throwing it away. When cities use both programs together, they can reduce landfill waste by half.
questions.prompt: Which text structure does this passage MAINLY use?
questions.explain: The passage presents a problem (too much landfill trash) and then offers solutions (recycling and composting). This is the problem-and-solution text structure.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Frogs and toads look similar, but they have key differences. Frogs have smooth, moist skin, while toads have dry, bumpy skin. Frogs usually live near water, whereas toads can live farther from it. Both are amphibians and help control insect populations.
questions.prompt: Which sentence from the passage shows the COMPARE AND CONTRAST structure?
options: Frogs have smooth, moist skin, while toads have dry, bumpy skin.
Both are amphibians and help control insect populations.
Frogs and toads look similar, but they have key differences.
questions.explain: The sentence uses the signal word 'while' to directly contrast two things (frogs vs. toads). This is the clearest example of compare-and-contrast structure in the passage.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Heavy rain caused the river to overflow its banks. As a result, the low-lying fields were flooded. Because of the flooding, farmers lost many of their crops.
questions.prompt: This passage is organized using CAUSE AND EFFECT. What is the FIRST cause?
questions.explain: The heavy rain is the first cause — it triggered the chain of effects: the river overflowed, fields flooded, and crops were lost.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: The old house at the end of Oak Street had not had visitors in years. Cobwebs hung from every corner. The floorboards creaked under each step. A single candle flickered in the upstairs window, though no one was known to live there.
questions.prompt: What mood does the author create in this passage?
questions.explain: Cobwebs, creaking floors, no visitors, and a flickering candle with no known resident all create a mysterious, eerie mood. The author uses these details to make the reader feel uneasy.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Kenji always wanted to win the art contest. He rushed his painting to finish first. When the results came in, his friend Priya — who had painted slowly and carefully — won first place. Kenji looked at his own painting and finally saw all the places he had rushed.
questions.prompt: What lesson does Kenji learn in this story?
options: Taking your time leads to better results
Winning contests is the most important thing
Painting is too hard for most people
questions.explain: Kenji rushed and his work was not as good. Priya took her time and won. The story teaches that doing something carefully — not rushing — leads to better results.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Scientists estimate that in 1900, about 3 times as many tigers lived in India as there are today. Today, there are approximately 2,500 tigers in India.
questions.prompt: Based on the passage, about how many tigers were there in India in 1900?
questions.explain: 3 times as many as today: 3 × 2,500 = 7,500 tigers. The passage says 1900 had about 3 times the current number.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: The school library has 4 shelves of fiction books and 3 shelves of nonfiction books. Each shelf holds 30 books. The librarian wants to add one more shelf of books and has 28 new books to add.
questions.prompt: How many books will be in the library AFTER the new shelf is added?
questions.explain: Current books: (4 + 3) × 30 = 7 × 30 = 210. New books to add: 28. Total = 210 + 28 = 238.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: A community garden has 6 plots. Each plot produces 8 pounds of vegetables per week. The garden donates half of all vegetables to a food bank.
questions.prompt: How many pounds of vegetables does the food bank receive each week?
questions.explain: Total vegetables = 6 × 8 = 48 pounds. Half donated = 48 ÷ 2 = 24 pounds to the food bank.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: The snow fell in a thick white blanket over the town. Every rooftop wore a white cap. The streets were silent except for the crunch of boots.
questions.prompt: In the phrase 'the snow fell in a thick white blanket,' what type of figurative language is used?
questions.explain: The snow is called a 'blanket' without using 'like' or 'as' — this is a metaphor. It compares the layer of snow to a blanket covering the town.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: The root 'scrib/script' means 'write.' Which word means 'a set of written instructions for a play or movie'?
questions.explain: 'Script' comes from 'scrib/script' meaning write. A script is a written document with lines and instructions for performers.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage:
Passage 1: The rainforest is home to more than half of the world's plant and animal species. Cutting down trees threatens these species with extinction.

Passage 2: In some regions, people depend on clearing rainforest land for farming to feed their families. Without this land, many communities would face hunger.
questions.prompt: Which statement describes how the two passages are DIFFERENT?
options: Passage 1 focuses on wildlife; Passage 2 focuses on human needs
Both passages argue for protecting the rainforest
Passage 2 supports protecting wildlife more than Passage 1
Both passages are about the same problem
questions.explain: Passage 1 is about the animals and plants living in the rainforest. Passage 2 is about people who need the land to grow food. They focus on different concerns.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Unlike cats, dogs need to be walked every day. Cats groom themselves, but dogs usually need regular baths. On the other hand, both animals make loving, loyal pets.
questions.prompt: What text structure is MAINLY used in this passage?
questions.explain: The passage uses signal words like 'unlike,' 'but,' and 'on the other hand' to show similarities and differences between cats and dogs. This is compare-and-contrast structure.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: After the long hike, Carlos gulped down two full water bottles. He sat on a log and didn't say a word for several minutes. His shoes were off before he even sat down.
questions.prompt: Which word BEST describes how Carlos feels after the hike?
questions.explain: Drinking two water bottles, sitting silently, and quickly removing shoes all suggest Carlos is very tired and exhausted after the hike.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Read this sentence: 'The pitcher walked to the mound.' Which meaning of 'pitcher' is used here?
options: A baseball player who throws the ball
A container used to pour liquid
A person who makes a sales presentation
questions.explain: Context clue: 'walked to the mound' (the pitcher's mound in baseball). In this sentence, 'pitcher' refers to the baseball player, not a container.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which sentence is INCORRECT?
options: The children plays outside every afternoon.
The child plays outside every afternoon.
The children play outside every afternoon.
Each child plays outside every afternoon.
questions.explain: 'Children' is plural, so the verb should be 'play' not 'plays.' The correct sentence is: The children play outside every afternoon.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: A school collected canned food for 3 weeks. In week 1, students collected 145 cans. In week 2, they collected twice as many cans as in week 1. In week 3, they collected 38 fewer cans than in week 2.
questions.prompt: How many cans did the school collect in total over the 3 weeks?
questions.explain: Week 1: 145 cans. Week 2: 2 × 145 = 290 cans. Week 3: 290 − 38 = 252 cans. Total = 145 + 290 + 252 = 687 cans.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: Every Saturday, Aisha volunteered at the animal shelter. She cleaned cages, walked dogs, and played with the cats. One day, a little girl came in and adopted the dog Aisha had been training for months. Aisha cried a little, but then she smiled — the dog finally had a home.
questions.prompt: Which sentence from the story BEST supports the theme 'Giving to others brings its own reward'?
options: Aisha cried a little, but then she smiled — the dog finally had a home.
Every Saturday, Aisha volunteered at the animal shelter.
She cleaned cages, walked dogs, and played with the cats.
A little girl came in and adopted the dog.
questions.explain: Aisha cried but then smiled knowing the dog found a home. This shows that her hard work and care — even though it meant giving up the dog she loved — brought her joy. That is the reward of giving.

questions.subject: reading
questions.passage: A farmer grows tomatoes and peppers. He has 9 rows of tomatoes with 8 plants in each row, and 6 rows of peppers with 7 plants in each row. He wants to know the total number of plants.
questions.prompt: What is the total number of plants on the farmer's land?
questions.explain: Tomato plants = 9 × 8 = 72. Pepper plants = 6 × 7 = 42. Total = 72 + 42 = 114 plants.
